Job Description Summary
Responsible for the coordination, planning, preparation,
presentation, and evaluation of all learning activities in any
given course. The instructor must remain current in the discipline
area and continually explore teaching methods and strategies to
engage learners, organize and plan instructional content that
accommodates diverse learning styles, and devise appropriate
assessment tools that monitor student learning outcomes. The
instructor is also responsible for participating in related
activities to include professional development, curriculum design,
and other activities that contribute to the department, division,
and College. The instructor performs all other duties as directed
by the Division Dean, EVP /Provost, or the President or
designee.
Minimum Qualifications
EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE
Master’s or doctoral degree in mathematics or a master’s or
doctoral degree in any discipline with a minimum of 15 graduate
credits in Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, or Statistics.
At least one year of teaching experience at the college level
in Mathematics, Algebra, Statistics, and/or STEM -related
mathematics or significant professional experience relevant to the
teaching area.
Teaching experience with respect to corequisite education
preferred.
Experience implementing high-impact teaching practices
preferred.
Criteria
CRITERIA : The following criteria, which are not the sole
criteria used in the final hiring decision, will be used to review
the applications of those persons who meet the stated minimum
qualifications and to select those qualified applicants who will be
interviewed. Other information and observations made during the
interview process may be considered in the selection process. A
Resume/CV and cover letter are required with the application.
Please ensure that your documents address the criteria listed below
for this position
ESSENTIAL DUTIES
Plan, organize, and teach curriculum content in support of
course outcomes.
Using applicable technology and andragogical principles, teach
course content via an appropriate delivery format (may include
face-to-face, hybrid, online, and remote instruction).
Complete mandated institutional trainings and professional
development as required.
Follow department and division requirements for preparing a
course syllabus.
Facilitate appropriate instructional activities that promote
student engagement and learning.
Evaluate student performance using assessment tools as directed
by the department, where appropriate; inform students in a timely
manner of their progress.
Provide an orientation at the first- class meeting to include
(as applicable) an overview of the course syllabus, an outline of
course objectives, course requirements, attendance policy, grading
system, textbook(s), and supplemental materials.
Notify students of key dates and course adjustments.
Comply with attendance and grading requirements as established
for the course (may include maintaining an up-to-date electronic
grade book and entering final grades by the established due
date).
Maintain accurate class records; submit required class records
by the established due date.
Participate in departmental evaluation and course assessment
processes as directed.
Follow department and division requirements for maintaining
office hours and referring students to appropriate resources.
Respond to student emails and phone calls within 48 hours with
the exception of weekends and holidays. Maintain regular
communication with students. Use the assigned PGCC email for
communication with the department and with students.
Submit annual program budgets to and work closely with the
appropriate Program Coordinator, Director or Program Director on
the development of annual division budgets for approval by the
Dean, if applicable.
Attend all required meetings.
Engage in appropriate and relevant service to the college and
to the department (e.g., search committees, faculty committees,
etc.)
Maintain the currency and relevance of all learning resources
for the courses, especially but not limited to OER’s
Perform all other job-related duties as assigned.
KNOWLEDGE SKILLS AND ABILITIES
Mastery of course content.
Demonstrable knowledge of Canvas, including the ability to
design, organize, and manage course materials, assignments, and
assessments within the platform effectively.
Ability to provide service to diverse populations using a
student-centered approach.
Ability to communicate effectively with students, faculty and
staff.
Ability to plan, deliver and assess effective instruction.
Ability to effectively use instructional technology (Internet,
instructional software, learning management system,
videoconferencing, etc.).
Critical thinking, organization, and conflict management
skills.
Research skills (where appropriate).
Time management, planning and organizational skills.
Ability to work as part of a team.
Problem-solving and analytical ability.
Ability to teach in non-traditional formats (online, remote,
hybrid) and settings (off-campus, weekends, evenings and
accelerated).
Job Requirements
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS
Must have the use of sensory skills in order to effectively
communicate and interact with other employees and the public
through the use of the telephone and personal contact as normally
defined by the ability to see, read, talk, hear, handle, or feel
objects and controls. Physical capability to effectively use and
operate various items of office related equipment, such as, but not
limited to a, personal computer, calculator, copier, and fax
machine. No significant climbing, stooping, kneeling, crouching,
reaching, standing, walking, pushing, pulling, lifting, grasping,
and repetitive motions.
OTHER REQUIREMENTS
Ability to communicate effectively in spoken and written
standard English.
As required by the 1986 Immigration Act, be prepared to present
acceptable documentation showing your identity and that you are a
U.S. citizen or an alien who is authorized to work.
A background investigation will be conducted prior to the offer
of employment. A signed authorization for the release of personal
information will be required if selected for an interview.
ACCOMMODATIONS
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to
satisfactorily perform each essential job duty. Prince George’s
Community College provides reasonable accommodations when requested
by a qualified applicant or employee with a disability, unless such

jobs.title: Assistant Professor -SOM Psych Adult
jobs.description:
Job Description
Faculty Opportunity
The University of Maryland School of Medicine, Department of
Psychiatry, is seeking qualified Adult Psychiatrists to provide
comprehensive psychiatric services across its acute and ambulatory
care programs at the Downtown University of Maryland Medical Center
(UMMC) campus. Positions are available on full-time basis and may
include opportunities to provide tele-mental health services in
support of the Department's expanding clinical programs. The
position carries a faculty appointment at the University and offers
an exciting opportunity for research, teaching and clinical work.
Academic rank and salary are commensurate with experience. Expected
rank is Assistant Professor or higher, however, rank and tenure
status is dependent on candidate’s qualifications.
Salary range for Assistant Professor MD, full-time 100% FTE:
$230,000-$250,000
The referenced salary range reflects base pay for Assistant
Professor which is based on faculty rank and years in rank. This
salary range does not include all components of the Department
faculty compensation program or pay from participation in
department variable compensation programs.
Therefore the actual compensation paid to the selected candidate
may vary from the salary range stated herein. For more information,
please contact the hiring department.
The referenced salary range represents the minimum and maximum
salaries for this position and is based on the University of
Maryland School of Medicine's good faith belief at the time of
posting. Not all candidates will be eligible for the upper end of
the salary range. The actual compensation offered to the selected
candidate may vary and will ultimately depend on multiple factors,
which may include the successful candidate's geographic location,
skills, work experience, internal equity, market conditions,
education/training and other factors, as reasonably determined by
the University.
UMB offers a comprehensive benefits package that prioritizes
wellness, work/life balance, and professional development. This
position offers a retirement program that must be selected and is
effective on your date of hire. Faculty receive a generous leave
package that includes over 4 weeks of vacation accrued each year,
paid holidays, personal leave, unlimited accrual of sick time, and
comprehensive health insurance; professional learning and
development programs; tuition remission for employees and their
dependents at any University System of Maryland school. Note: Leave
and tuition benefits are prorated for part-time employees.
UMB is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will
receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender
identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national
origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other
characteristic protected by law or policy. If you need a reasonable
accommodation for a disability for any part of the employment
process, please submit an online request or contact
HRDiversity@umaryland.edu Please note that only inquiries
concerning a request for reasonable accommodation will be responded
to from this email address.
.
Responsibilities
Faculty members will provide psychiatric evaluations, treatment,
and ongoing management of adult patients with a range of
psychiatric conditions. In addition to clinical responsibilities,
faculty will contribute to the Department's academic mission
through teaching, research, and interdisciplinary collaboration.
The positions include faculty appointments at the University of
Maryland School of Medicine, with access to departmental mentoring
and professional development opportunities.
Qualifications
Doctorate or recognized terminal degree in the field of
specialization. Shown potential for superior teaching, service, and
research, scholarship, or r creative performance, commensurate with
the mission of the UMB. May require unrestricted license in the
State of Maryland. Candidates must be ABPN certified or
eligible.

jobs.title: Anesthesia, Clinical or Tenure Track Assistant/Associate/Full Professor
jobs.description:
Job Description
Overview
The Department of Clinical Sciences at the Auburn University
College of Veterinary Medicine is seeking applicants to fill a
full-time, 12-month/year appointment. Depending on experience,
qualifications, and interest, the successful candidate will be
appointed to either a tenure-track (Assistant/Associate/Professor)
or a non-tenure-track (Clinical Assistant/Associate/Professor)
position in anesthesia.
Responsibilities
The successful candidate will be expected to participate in
teaching, clinical service, and research/scholarly activity.
Teaching responsibilities include the clinical, didactic, and
laboratory instructional activities of professional veterinary
medicine and postgraduate training programs related to anesthesia.
Full-time equivalent (FTE) assignments for clinical service and
research responsibilities are negotiable and will depend on the
successful candidate’s interests and the type of appointment, i.e.,
clinical vs. tenure track. Clinical service expectations include
teaching professional veterinary students, residents, and interns
while providing anesthesia services for the Bailey Small Animal
Teaching Hospital and for the JT Vaughan Large Animal Teaching
hospital. After-hours duties are shared among the faculty and
consist of backing up the primary on-call residents. Board-eligible
faculty will be provided with dedicated time for certifying exam
preparation.
Qualifications
Applicants for the position must hold a DVM or equivalent degree;
and be either board-eligible or have obtained Diplomate status in
the American College of Veterinary Anesthesia and Analgesia (ACVAA)
or the European College of Veterinary Anaesthesia and Analgesia
(ECVAA). These qualifications must be met at the time employment
begins. The candidate selected for this position must be able to
meet eligibility requirements to work in the United States at the
time the appointment is scheduled to begin and continue working
legally for the proposed term of employment. Eligibility for
faculty veterinary licensure in the State of Alabama is also
required.
For a tenure-track position, research experience and an advanced
degree (MS or PhD) are desired but not required. Tenure-track
faculty are expected to establish a specific area of research
focus, seek extramural funding, and mentor residents pursuing
graduate degrees.
Description of anesthesiology service: The successful
applicant will join a team of four ACVAA Diplomate faculty, five
ACVAA residents, and eight technicians. The anesthesia service
supports specialists in small animal medicine and surgery; equine
medicine and surgery; food animal medicine and surgery; avian and
exotic medicine; theriogenology, dairy medicine; sports medicine;
emergency and critical care; medical, surgical and radiation
oncology; ophthalmology; cardiology; dermatology; neurology;
community practice/dentistry; and diagnostic imaging.
Small animal anesthesia equipment includes integrated Mindray Veta
5 and Veta 3 with Mindray multi-parameter monitors (including agent
monitoring), Surgivet CDS-9000 workstations with DRE
multi-parameter monitors (including agent monitoring), Datex-Ohmeda
Aestiva 3000 anesthesia workstation with S5 multi-parameter
monitor, Hallowell ventilators, Sonosite ultrasound machine,
peripheral nerve stimulators, Phillips Expression MR compatible
multi-parameter monitor, DRE MR compatible small animal anesthesia
machine with ventilator, and NOVA blood gas analyzer. Large animal
anesthesia equipment includes Hallowell Tafonius Jr. anesthesia
machines, JD Medical LAV-3000 MRI compatible large animal
anesthesia machine, Aestiva 3000 anesthesia workstation, two DRE
multi-parameter monitors and NOVA blood gas analyzer. Other
equipment onsite includes Co2 surgical laser (Aesculight), Eklin
digital radiology, linear accelerator, 3T Phillips MRI, GE
128-slice CT scan (both with large and small animal capabilities),
standing equine CT, a Siemens digital RF suite, and GE
interventional radiology suite. The Auburn University MRI center
provides 3T and 7T MRI service for research studies. The small
animal and large animal ICU facilities are approved for ACVECC
training and have dialysis capabilities.
For a virtual tour of the facilities, please see these
videos:
Auburn Vet Med Small Animal Teaching
Hospital
Auburn Vet Med Large Animal
Hospital
Minimum Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
None.
Contract Type
Continuing
Application Instructions
Applications for this position must include 1) a letter of intent
stating the candidate’s strengths and professional goals, 2) a
current curriculum vitae, and 3) names, email addresses, and
telephone numbers of three professional references.
Candidates interested in a tenure-track position must provide a
research statement describing their primary research interests and
research goals. Candidates interested in a clinical-track must
provide a statement describing collaborative research, teaching, or
other scholarly interests.
General inquiries may be directed to Stuart Clark-Price, Professor
of Anesthesia and Search Committee Chair (scc0066@auburn.edu).
Starting salary will be commensurate with experience and
credentials.
Review of applications will commence on January 4, 2027 and will
continue until a qualified applicant is recommended for
appointment.
Auburn University is understanding and sensitive to the family
needs of faculty, including dual-career couples. http://www.auburn.edu/academic/provost/facultyjobs/
Why Work at Auburn?
Teaching, Research, and Scholarship Opportunities: Shared
research space and technical support, including a clinical trials
coordinator, are provided within the Department. There are numerous
opportunities for research collaboration within the Auburn
University veterinary medicine campus, Auburn University’s main
campus, and the Edward Via College of Osteopathic Medicine Auburn
campus as well as at medical colleges at the University of Alabama
at Birmingham and Emory University. The Department participates in
college-wide veterinary and graduate programs. Faculty development
is a priority, and guided, structured mentorship will be provided
to support the career development and professional growth of new
faculty through the formal mentoring program in the Department of
Clinical Sciences. The Biggio Center for the Enhancement of
Teaching and Learning (wp.auburn.edu/biggio) located on Auburn’s
main campus is an invaluable resource for all things teaching
related including support for instructional technologies. The CVM
also has monthly teaching enhancement workshops and a summer
teaching institute that has brought nationally recognized speakers
to present on a variety of teaching related topics. The AU-CVM is
supported by a medical and scientific research library,
professionally staffed and with computer, video and other research
support facilities. Faculty are provided with photocopying
privileges, inter-library loan services, and photographic services.
Many electronic books are available through the AU-CVM library
including several major anesthesiology textbooks. Journal articles
are maintained in the AU-CVM on-site library, or available through
interlibrary loan request with ease.
For more information about the College of Veterinary Medicine,
please reference our website at https://www.vetmed.auburn.edu/ .
The University: Auburn University is one of the nation’s
premier public land-grant institutions. In the 2027 U.S. News &
World Report, Auburn ranked #46 among top public institutions.
Auburn maintains high levels of research activity and high
standards for teaching excellence, offering Bachelor’s, Master’s,
Educational Specialist, and Doctor’s degrees in agriculture and
engineering, the professions, and the arts and sciences. Its
2025-26 enrollment of 35,733 students includes 29,693
undergraduates and 6,040 graduate and professional students.
Organized into twelve academic colleges and schools, Auburn’s 1,552
faculty members offer more than 200 educational programs. The
University is nationally recognized for its commitment to academic
excellence and community engagement, its positive work environment,
its thriving student life programs, and its beautiful campus.
Auburn University offers a wealth of benefits to its employees, to
remain competitive in an ever-changing landscape of academia. More
information about employee benefits and tiger Perks can be viewed
here: https://auburn.edu/administration/human_resources/benefits/index.php
The Area: Auburn residents enjoy a thriving community,
recognized as one of the “best small towns in America,” and one of
the “top ten small towns in the South” with moderate climate and
easy access to major cities or to beach and mountain recreational
facilities. Situated along the rapidly developing I-85 corridor
between Atlanta, Georgia, and Montgomery, Alabama, the combined
Auburn-Opelika-Columbus statistical area has a population of over
500,000, with excellent public-school systems and regional medical
centers. The town has an art museum, performing arts center, and
many regional opportunities for music and theater performances.
Numerous cultural and recreational venues and idyllic escapes are
within one hour of Auburn including Callaway Gardens, the Alabama
Shakespeare Festival, and numerous shopping and dining experiences.
Clement weather allows for extensive outdoor recreational
opportunities including trails for walking or cycling,
kayaking/boating in the many rivers that traverse the area and in
Lake Martin with its 600 miles of shoreline, Tuskegee National
Forest and other State Parks, all within a short drive from
downtown. The 240,000 square foot university recreation center and
multiple indoor lap pools and outdoor lounging pools offer
additional opportunities to facilitate a healthy active lifestyle.
Additional information can be found at https://www.aotourism.com/top-reasons-to-love-auburn-and-opelika/
.
Ready to lead and shape the future of higher education? Apply
today! War Eagle!

opportunities for all individuals without regard to race, color,

jobs.title: Chair of the School of Computational Science and Engineering (CSE)
jobs.institution: Georgia Institute of Technology, College of Computing
jobs.description:
The College of Computing at the Georgia Institute of Technology invites applications and nominations from qualified individuals for the position of Chair of the School of Computational Science and Engineering (CSE). The School of CSE is one of the nation's first inherently interdisciplinary departments devoted to the study and advancement of computational methods and data-driven methods for understanding natural and engineered systems. The new Chair will be expected to further build upon the many accomplishments, professional relationships, and interdisciplinary strides that already exist in the School by providing strategic vision and effective leadership.
The College of Computing was established in 1990 as one of the first Colleges of Computing in the nation at an R1 university and is a world-class leader in research and computing breakthroughs, with such programs as Threads and multiple Online Masters of Science degrees. Its graduate program is currently ranked 8th nationally by U.S. News & World Report, as well as 8th in the world by The Times Higher Education World University Ranking. The College of Computing comprises five schools, which provide specialized and general computing education to the entire campus. Located in the heart of Atlanta, GA, the College is part of the Georgia Institute of Technology, which is a unit of the University System of the State of Georgia.
The School of CSE, housed in the newly-opened CODA building, participates in, and offers, bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees. The School has garnered $7.5M in new research expenditures and $34M in active awards for FY2026, reaching an average level of over $1.1M per faculty member in research expenditures. A new $5.3M High-Performance Computing system supports 50 faculty and more than 200 students working on topics including astrophysics, computational biology, and health sciences.
CSE faculty and students have access to a $44 million NSF-supported Nexus resource for artificial intelligence and scientific computing. Nexus provides CSE with a significant platform for interdisciplinary research, education, and collaboration across science, engineering, health, and other computationally intensive domains. The School currently has 28 academic faculty (including joint appointments), in addition to numerous research scientists, postdoctoral fellows, and adjunct faculty. It also has 116 M.S. students and 104 Ph.D. students. Disciplines associated with the School include high-performance computing, machine learning and artificial intelligence, data science and engineering, cybersecurity, modeling and simulation, visualization, and numerical and discrete algorithms, with applications in a variety of science, engineering, health, and social domains.
The CSE Chair reports to the John P. Imlay Dean of Computing and is responsible for all administrative, budgetary, and personnel decisions within the School. The Chair also provides leadership in setting the vision, strategic direction, and goals for the School.
We seek candidates with a strong commitment to education, a distinguished research and funding record, and a proven ability to work well with a diverse group of faculty, staff, and students, as well as other campus administrators and leaders. Specifically, the chair would be responsible for developing and executing a communication strategy for increasing the visibility of CSE. An ideal candidate should have an inspiring vision for the future of CSE and possess the following characteristics: exceptional academic standing in the field; collegial approach to problem solving and conflict resolution; ability to bring together faculty with diverse interests; openness in decision-making; strong organizational, team-building, and decision-making skills; experience with people and fiscal management, strategic planning, and vision development; and commitment to personal and educational enrichment of its faculty, staff, and students.
Candidates for this position should have a doctorate in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, and be appointed at the rank of full professor (or equivalent) in a leading research university or research organization.
To apply, candidates must visit https://academicjobsonline.org/ajo/jobs/33373 complete the online application form, which requires electronic submission of the candidate's latest CV, a letter of application, 5 references with names, phone numbers, and physical and email addresses, along with other supporting documents. This search will commence immediately and will continue until the position is filled. Review of applications will begin on January 15, 2027.
ABOUT US
Overview
Georgia Tech prides itself on its technological resources, collaborations, high-quality student body, and its commitment to building an outstanding and diverse community of learning, discovery, and creation. We strongly encourage applicants whose values align with our institutional values, as outlined in our strategic plan. These values include academic excellence, diversity of thought and experience, inquiry and innovation, collaboration and community, and ethical behavior and stewardship. Georgia Tech has policies to promote a healthy work-life balance and is aware that attracting faculty may require meeting the needs of two careers.
About Georgia Tech
Georgia Tech is a top-ranked public research university situated in the heart of Atlanta, a diverse and vibrant city with numerous economic and cultural strengths. The Institute serves more than 45,000 students through top-ranked undergraduate, graduate, and executive programs in engineering, computing, science, business, design, and liberal arts. Georgia Tech's faculty attracted more than $1.4 billion in research awards this past year in fields ranging from biomedical technology to artificial intelligence, energy, sustainability, semiconductors, neuroscience, and national security. Georgia Tech ranks among the nation's top 20 universities for research and development spending and No. 1 among institutions without a medical school.
Georgia Tech's Mission and Values
Georgia Tech's mission is to develop leaders who advance technology and improve the human condition. The Institute has nine key values that are foundational to everything we do:
1. Students are our top priority.
2. We strive for excellence.
3. We thrive on diversity.
4. We celebrate collaboration.
5. We champion innovation.
6. We safeguard freedom of inquiry and expression.
7. We nurture the wellbeing of our community.
8. We act ethically.
9. We are responsible stewards.
Over the next decade, Georgia Tech will become an example of inclusive innovation, a leading technological research university of unmatched scale, relentlessly committed to serving the public good; breaking new ground in addressing the biggest local, national, and global challenges and opportunities of our time; making technology broadly accessible; and developing exceptional, principled leaders from all backgrounds ready to produce novel ideas and create solutions with real human impact.
CONTACT INFORMATION
For additional information about this job opening, please contact the Search Chair, Prof. Kishore Ramachandran, at rama@gatech.edu.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
Doctorate degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, Science, or a related field.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
The ideal candidate should possess effective communication, leadership, and organizational skills. Experience leading a school or department within a technical institute or a STEM-focused research university is preferred.
The qualities and attributes of the successful candidate for the chair include:
Full Professorship with tenure in a premier department at a research university or have an equivalent position in industry or government in a discipline relevant to Computational Science and Engineering, such as Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, or Science
Demonstrated strong leadership and team building skills
Care about the personal and educational enrichment of faculty, staff, and students
Experience with strategic planning, administrative oversight, fiscal management, and vision development
Embrace participative management and transparent decision-making.
REQUIRED DOCUMENTS TO ATTACH
Applicants should submit:
A letter of application
Current curriculum vitae
The names and contact information for five references, including phone numbers, physical addresses, and email addresses, along with other supporting documents.
OTHER INFORMATION
For more details about the position, please visit: https://www.cc.gatech.edu/chair-search-computational-science-and-engineering.
BACKGROUND CHECK
A successful candidate must be able to pass a background check. Please visit: https://usg.policystat.com/policy/19298143/latest.
USG CORE VALUES
The University System of Georgia is comprised of our 25 institutions of higher education and learning as well as the System Office. Our USG Statement of Core Values are Integrity, Excellence, Accountability, and Respect. These values serve as the foundation for all that we do as an organization, and each USG community member is responsible for demonstrating and upholding these standards. More details on the USG Statement of Core Values and Code of Conduct are available in USG Board Policy 8.2.18.1.2 and can be found on-line at https://www.usg.edu/policymanual/section8/C224/#p8.2.18_personnel_conduct.
Additionally, USG supports Freedom of Expression as stated in Board Policy 6.5 Freedom of Expression and Academic Freedom found on-line at https://www.usg.edu/policymanual/section6/C2653.
EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY
The Georgia Institute of Technology (Georgia Tech) is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. The Institute is committed to maintaining a fair and respectful environment for all. To that end, and in accordance with federal and state law, Board of Regents policy, and Institute policy, Georgia Tech provides equal opportunity to all faculty, staff, students, and all other members of the Georgia Tech community, including applicants for admission and/or employment, contractors, volunteers, and participants in institutional programs, activities, or services. Georgia Tech complies with all applicable laws and regulations governing equal opportunity in the workplace and in educational activities.
Equal opportunity and decisions based on merit are fundamental values of the University System of Georgia ("USG") and Georgia Tech. Georgia Tech prohibits discrimination, including discriminatory harassment, on the basis of an individual's race, ethnicity, ancestry, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, age, disability, genetics, or veteran status in its programs, activities, employment, and admissions. Further, Georgia Tech prohibits citizenship status, immigration status, and national origin discrimination in hiring, firing, and recruitment, except where such restrictions are required in order to comply with law, regulation, executive order, or Attorney General directive, or where they are required by Federal, State, or local government contract.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Mathematics
jobs.description:
Position Summary
Batten University invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor of Mathematics in the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science within the Joan P. Brock School of Mathematics and Natural Sciences, beginning August 2027.
The successful candidate will demonstrate a commitment to excellence in undergraduate teaching, student engagement, scholarly and professional development, and academic service. The faculty member will be responsible for delivering high-quality instruction, advising and mentoring students, contributing to curriculum development, maintaining scholarly and professional activity, and participating in departmental and University service.
The successful candidate will foster an engaging and inclusive learning environment that promotes student success and advances the academic mission of Batten University.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
-Teach undergraduate courses in Mathematics supporting the University's Mathematics and Data Science majors, as well as general education requirements.
-Teach courses in Computer Science as appropriate to departmental needs and individual qualifications.
-Teach six courses per academic year within the University's 4-1-4 academic calendar.
-Provide academic advising and mentoring to students to support their academic and professional development.
-Contribute to curriculum development and enhancement, including potential development of courses within the Data Science program.
-Develop, evaluate, and revise academic courses and instructional materials to support departmental and University objectives.
-Maintain scholarly and professional activity consistent with expectations for tenure-track faculty.
-Participate in departmental meetings, faculty committees, and University service activities.
-Collaborate with faculty and academic leadership to support student learning, academic program development, and institutional initiatives.
-Demonstrate a commitment to effective teaching practices that integrate academic theory with practical application.
-Perform other related academic and departmental responsibilities as assigned.
Required Qualifications
-Earned Ph.D. in Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, or Data Science.
-Demonstrated commitment to excellence in undergraduate teaching and student engagement.
-Ability to teach undergraduate Mathematics courses supporting departmental and general education requirements.
-Commitment to academic advising, student mentorship, and professional development.
-Ability to contribute to departmental and University service.
Preferred Qualifications
-Demonstrated university-level teaching experience.
-Professional experience or technical expertise related to Data Science.
-Relevant professional certifications or licenses.
-Experience developing or enhancing undergraduate curriculum, particularly in Mathematics or Data Science.
-Ability to teach undergraduate courses in Computer Science.
-Demonstrated record of effective teaching and an educational philosophy that integrates theory and practice.

Department: Mathematics and Computer Science
Faculty Status: Tenure-track
Rank: Assistant Professor
FLSA Classification: Exempt – Teaching Professional
Anticipated Start Date: August 2027
Teaching Load: Six courses per academic year (4-1-4 academic calendar)
Salary: Competitive and commensurate with qualifications and experience
Work Location: Batten University, Virginia Beach, Virginia

Interested candidates should apply through the Batten University Employment Opportunities webpage.
Applicants must submit the following materials as PDF attachments:
-Cover letter.
-Current curriculum vitae.
-List of at least three professional references, including each reference's title and contact information.
-Statement of teaching philosophy.
-Statement describing experience teaching students from diverse backgrounds.
-Graduate transcripts (unofficial transcripts are acceptable during the initial application process).
Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled.
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
Batten University is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Applicants are considered on the basis of skills, experience, and qualifications without regard to race, religion, color, creed, gender, national or ethnic origin, age, marital status, covered veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, the presence of a non-job-related disability, or any other legally protected status.

The School of Engineering includes seven academic departments and 10 engineering majors, offering exceptional opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration and innovation. We seek outstanding scholars whose work advances one or more of our strategic priority areas: Physical and Virtual Infrastructure, Healthcare Technology, Innovations in Energy, Defense and National Security, and Experiential Learning and Professional Education. Appointments may be made in one or more engineering departments based on the candidate’s expertise and interests.
Rutgers University–New Brunswick’s School of Engineering is home to educational opportunity and innovation, preparing a richly diverse body of nearly 6,000 undergraduate and graduate students to solve problems, make meaningful societal advances, lead through innovation, and excel in the global workplace. Ranked among the leading engineering programs in the nation, the school is centrally located in the Northeast Corridor amid a powerhouse of industrial, pharmaceutical, high-tech, transportation, and financial industries, providing professional and research opportunities. jobs.title: Director Strategic Faculty Recruitment (Office of the Provost)
jobs.description:
Job Details
Johns Hopkins, founded in 1876, is America's first research
university and home to nine world-class academic divisions working
together as one university.
We are seeking an experienced and strategic Director
Strategic Faculty Recruitment, a senior-level leader who
will build a new central function and lead its recruitment team, to
support faculty recruitment and hiring across ambitious
interdisciplinary institutional initiatives at Johns Hopkins
University. The Director Strategic Faculty Recruitment will serve
as a strategic partner to academic and program leaders, providing
expertise in recruitment operations, pipeline management, candidate
stewardship, process improvement, and institutional coordination.
The position will scope and hire additional positions to support
this function and provides a consistent point of coordination for
candidates from first engagement through acceptance and arrival.
This is a newly established function at Johns Hopkins, and the
successful candidate will have the opportunity to shape it from the
ground up: designing its operating model, recruiting and developing
its team, and building the processes, tools, and relationships that
will support faculty hiring across the university for years to
come. The function is expected to grow as institutional needs
evolve.
The successful candidate will work closely with academic
leaders, Faculty Affairs, Development and Alumni Relations,
Research, Human Resources, Finance, and school and departmental
leadership to strengthen recruitment execution. Academic units and
program leads retain responsibility for evaluating and selecting
candidates; this role coordinates and supports that work. This
position will report to the Senior Associate Vice Provost for
Strategy & Operations and Chief of Staff in the Provost's
Office during the implementation phase; the permanent
organizational home is the Office of Faculty Affairs, with timing
of the transition to be determined.
Specific Duties & Responsibilities
Faculty Recruitment Strategy and Operations
Serve as a strategic partner to academic and program leaders on
faculty recruitment strategies, processes, timelines, and
execution.
Advise hiring leaders and stakeholders on recruitment practices
and help identify and address barriers affecting faculty
searches.
Establish consistent recruitment processes, tools, and
practices across major institutional hiring initiatives.
Define a common recruitment lifecycle (for example, Source,
Engage, Nurture, Assess, Offer, Hire) with stage definitions, entry
and exit criteria, owners, and sub-steps, in partnership with
academic program leads.
Work with academic program leads, deans, and approvers so that
offer parameters, approval paths, and resource authority are agreed
upon in advance.
Establish regular coordination with academic program leads to
monitor recruitment activity and address emerging challenges.
Recruitment Pipeline Management and Reporting
Develop and maintain recruitment pipelines, tracking tools,
dashboards, and reporting structures across major hiring
initiatives.
Maintain a single shared tracker showing, for each active
candidate, the named owner, current stage, last move, dated next
move, and open risks, and lead a standing pipeline review.
Monitor recruitment milestones, including candidate pipelines,
visits, seminars, offers, approvals, and completed hires.
Track metrics that guide action, including candidates per
stage, time in stage, conversion between stages, offer acceptance
rate, and reasons for declines, and report progress against annual
and program hiring goals and gift milestones, in coordination with
DAR.
Provide timely information and analysis regarding recruitment
progress, hiring goals, emerging risks, and external talent market
trends and competitive hiring conditions.
Support realistic recruitment planning and goal setting based
on recruitment activity, timelines, and institutional
capacity.
Candidate Stewardship and Engagement
Provide, or designate and oversee, a consistent point of
coordination for each candidate from first engagement through
acceptance and arrival, so candidates know whom to contact and what
comes next.
Coordinate candidate communications so that outreach from
faculty, chairs, deans, program leads, and other senior leaders is
timely, consistent, and personalized.
Partner with deans, program leads, and Development and Alumni
Relations to develop compelling recruitment materials and a
consistent Hopkins value proposition.
Time and coordinate senior leader involvement, such as calls,
visits, and resource commitments, to the moments that most
influence a candidate's decision.
Work with the teams to ensure successful campus visits.
Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to support
dual career recruitments and opportunities
Ensure that sensitive candidate information is handled
confidentially, with role-based access.
Team Leadership and Function Building
Develop, lead, and supervise the recruitment team
Assign candidates and programs to team members, set
expectations for each pipeline stage, and review team workload
against pipeline volume.
Oversee team support for candidate touchpoints, visit
logistics, and search committee coordination
Recommend when additional recruiter capacity is needed, based
on factors such as active candidates per recruiter, time in stage,
and program hiring goals.
Lead the recruitment, selection, and onboarding of team
members.
Set goals for each team member, hold regular check-ins and
performance evaluations, and support professional development.
Foster a collaborative, service-oriented team culture grounded
in discretion, responsiveness, and accountability.
Design the function's operating model and staffing plan, and
lead long-term planning for additional staff and expanded
capabilities as the function evolves.
Institutional Coordination and Reporting
Serve as a central point of coordination among academic
leaders, program teams, Faculty Affairs, Development and Alumni
Relations, Research, Human Resources, Finance, and other university
partners involved in faculty recruitment.
Support institutional reporting and philanthropic stewardship
by maintaining accurate information regarding faculty hiring
commitments and progress against gift milestones, in coordination
with DAR.
Identify opportunities to improve recruitment processes and
develop recommendations that strengthen the university's long-term
capacity for faculty hiring.
Facilitate coordination across initiatives when recruitment
activities, candidates, or institutional processes intersect.
Special Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
Strong knowledge of faculty recruitment practices, academic
hiring processes, and higher education organizational
structures.
Demonstrated ability to serve as a trusted advisor and
strategic partner to senior academic and administrative
leaders.
Strong project management and organizational skills, with the
ability to manage multiple recruitment initiatives
simultaneously.
Strong analytical skills and ability to translate recruitment
data and complex information into clear insights and
recommendations.
Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication
skills.
Demonstrated ability to build relationships and influence
across a decentralized organization.
Strong judgment, discretion, and ability to manage sensitive
and confidential information.
Demonstrated ability to build, lead, develop, and supervise a
high-performing team, including establishing a new function or
office.
Experience engaging and building relationships with prospective
candidates, including senior or distinguished faculty.
Expertise in executive search methodologies and candidate
sourcing strategies.
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree.
Eight years of experience in recruitment, executive
recruitment, academic administration, advancement, or a related
field involving candidate relationship management with
progressively increasing responsibility.
Demonstrated experience supervising staff, including hiring,
goal setting, performance management, and professional
development.
Experience managing complex, cross-functional initiatives
involving multiple senior stakeholders.
Experience developing recruitment dashboards, metrics,
reporting systems, or other recruitment infrastructure.
Additional education may substitute for required experience and
additional related experience may substitute for required education
beyond a high school diploma/graduation equivalent, to the extent
permitted by the JHU equivalency formula.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience in academic administration, higher education
strategy, or related fields.
Working familiarity with faculty appointment, voting, tenure,
startup, space, and dual-career processes.
Experience working directly with faculty, department chairs,
deans, or other senior academic leaders.
Experience managing faculty recruitment pipelines or
institutional faculty hiring initiatives.
Experience working across decentralized organizations and
developing new processes or infrastructure.
Experience with moves management, talent pipelining, or
candidate relationship management practices or systems.
Experience recruiting senior faculty or academic leaders at a
research university or academic medical center.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Rank: Assistant Professor
Department: Ethnic Studies
Starting Date: Fall 2027
The Ethnic Studies Program at California State University San
Marcos (CSUSM) invites applications for a tenure-track faculty
position at the level of Assistant Professor. We seek a candidate
whose teaching, research, and community and professional service
are grounded in critical, comparative, and/or relational Ethnic
Studies, with a specialization in Black Studies. We particularly
welcome candidates whose research and teaching focus on African
American history, politics, and cultural production.
The B.A. in Ethnic Studies provides an interdisciplinary education
in critical, comparative, and relational approaches to Black,
Indigenous, Chicanx and Latinx, and Asian American Studies. In
centering the histories, lived experiences, and cultural
productions of historically marginalized communities, Ethnic
Studies trains students in theories and methods that emphasize
community-based and liberatory approaches to knowledge production
and critical inquiry. Through pedagogies of care, social justice,
and empowerment, Ethnic Studies scholars and students develop a
diverse set of tools to respond to the most pressing needs of our
communities. We theorize and intervene in multiple structures of
power—such as racism, settler colonialism, heteropatriarchy, and
empire—in dialogue and collaboration with social movements,
activists, and artists. Guided by three foundational principles
relaying back to the historic Third World Liberation Strike in
1968—solidarity, self-determination, and relevant education—we
serve the growth of future leaders in local, national, and
transnational contexts.
The successful candidate will be expected to develop and teach
courses for undergraduate majors and minors in Ethnic Studies, and
for students looking to fulfill the CSU Subject Area 6 General
Education Requirement— i.e. CSU Ethnic Studies Graduation
Requirement, to develop an active and sustainable research and/or

interdisciplinary field with a specialization in Black Studies ;

and/or creative activity agenda.
Demonstrated commitment to working effectively with our student

relevant/aligned interdisciplinary fields.

Studies.
Demonstrated ability to develop and teach undergraduate courses
in critical, comparative, and relational Ethnic Studies and Black
Studies and to develop and teach courses with respect to
candidate's research specializations.
Demonstrated record for innovative, high-impact, and culturally
responsive approaches to teaching and mentoring.
Demonstrated record of conducting, publishing, and/or
presenting research and/or creative activity to academic and/or
nonacademic audiences.
Demonstrated record of planning and coordinating
community-based and/or public-facing programs, initiatives, and/or
projects.

comparative and/or relational Ethnic Studies, and additional
area(s) of specialization;

that will lead to publications and other forms of knowledge
production and circulation;
Contribute significantly to curriculum and program
development;
Participate in meaningful departmental, college, university,
community and/or professional service.

jobs.title: Open Rank Positions (tenure and tenure track) spanning Quantitative Methods & Data Analytics
jobs.institution: Peabody College of Education and Human Development
jobs.description:
Vanderbilt’s Peabody College of Education and Human Development together with Vanderbilt’s College of Connected Computing (CCC) invites applicants for 2 open rank (tenure or tenure-track) faculty positions in Generative AI (GenAI) Psychometrics with joint appointments in both the Quantitative Methods & Data Analytics Program within Peabody College and the CCC. The CCC, Vanderbilt’s first new college in 40 years, merges data science, computer science, and statistical computing.
We seek a candidate publishing innovative generative AI psychometrics research within methodological journals who can train Ph.D. students in these methods. Examples of research areas bridging QMDA and CCC might include, for instance, developing or psychometrically evaluating methods for using large language models (LLMs) in item generation, improving and evaluating the reliability and validity of AI models for, e.g., emotion detection, creating psychometric tools for critiquing and designing large language model benchmarks, and/or adapting psychometric methods to compare simulated questionnaire responses from AI models versus humans to further our understanding of whether the same constructs are being measured by each. That is, candidates might be, for example, developing psychometric methods and tools to assess how well LLM benchmarks perform, how well LLMs generate items to measure a construct, how well LLMs score participant responses, or how well LLMs respond to measures in place of participants. A methodological specialization with broad application and connection to ongoing research at Peabody College is desirable, as is a capacity for effectively presenting complex technical content in a clear and understandable manner. A candidate should have an excellent record of research productivity, be developing an impactful program of methodological research, have a strong commitment to mentoring and inclusive teaching of a diverse population of students at the graduate and undergraduate levels, have potential for securing external funding, and have an earned doctorate in quantitative behavioral/social science methods or a related data science discipline.
We particularly welcome applicants who are interested in teaching methodological courses focusing on AI that complement and expand the existing QMDA program offerings, and who are also interested in contributing to other methodological teaching needs in both P&HD and CCC. The candidate’s tenure home will be in Peabody College and they will also be a core faculty member in the CCC, reinforcing ongoing connections between Peabody College and the CCC, and potentially fostering collaborations across colleges.
Beyond Vanderbilt’s CCC and Peabody’s QMDA Program, there is a wealth of additional quantitative expertise embedded in the wider Vanderbilt community for networking, collaboration, and faculty development. This includes: Biostatistics, the Data Science Institute, Biomedical Data Science and AI, and Scientific Computing, as well as a broad commitment to teaching excellence supported by our Institute for the Advancement of Higher Education. Vanderbilt University’s main campus is located in Nashville, TN, one of the fastest-growing and culturally rich metropolitan areas in the U.S., and ranked in 2026 as a best place to live. Peabody is one of the top-five Colleges of Education and Human Development in the U.S., with relatively small class sizes, competitive salary, and excellent benefits.
Application review will begin immediately; you are encouraged to complete your application promptly for earliest consideration.
Applications should be submitted to https://apply.interfolio.com/198028
Applications received by December 20, 2026 will receive full consideration. Applications should include a cover letter, curriculum vitae, at least 3 letters of recommendation, a research statement, teaching/mentoring statement, and relevant additional supplemental material (e.g., at least three manuscripts, student evaluation summaries, etc.). Requests for information should be sent to search chair Sonya Sterba sonya.sterba@vanderbilt.edu.
Vanderbilt University shall abide by the requirements of 41 CFR §§ 60-1.4(a), 60-300.5(a) and 60-741.5(a). These regulations prohibit discrimination against qualified individuals based on their status as protected veterans or individuals with disabilities, and prohibit discrimination against all individuals based on their race, color, religion, sex, or national origin. Moreover, these regulations require that covered prime contractors and subcontractors take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment individuals without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, protected veteran status or disability.

jobs.title: Principal Faculty - Physician Assistant Institute
jobs.description:
Job Details
The mission of The University of Bridgeport is to promote
academic excellence, personal responsibility, and commitment to
service. Distinctive curricula in an international, culturally
diverse, supportive learning environment prepare graduates for life
and leadership in an increasingly interconnected world.
Position Description Summary/Purpose:
The University of Bridgeport seeks a full-time Principal Faculty
member for the Physician Assistant Institute. Reporting to the
Program Director, this 12-month position is designated as principal
faculty under ARC-PA definitions and supports the Institute’s
educational, administrative, and accreditation activities. Academic
rank and salary are commensurate with scholarly achievement,
teaching, and clinical experience.
The position requires a five-day workweek, including four days
on-site at the Physician Assistant Institute and a fifth day
dedicated to clinical practice or professional advancement and
contribution. The expected faculty workload is 15 credits per term,
with release time for assigned responsibilities, subject to
university workload policy and HR confirmation.
Essential Job Functions/Primary Responsibilities:
(The essential functions or duties listed below are intended
only as illustrations of the various types of work that may be
performed. The omission of specific statements of duties does not
exclude them from the position if the work is similar, related, or
a logical assignment to the position.)
General Principal Faculty Responsibilities
Program Mission and Goals (A2.05a): Participate
in developing, reviewing, and revising the program mission
statement, goals, and competencies.
Admissions (A2.05b): Participate in applicant
evaluation and selection for admission to the PA program.
Student Instruction (A2.05c): Provide student
instruction in assigned didactic and clinical educational
activities.
Student Evaluation (A2.05d): Evaluate student
performance using appropriate assessment methods and document
results.
Academic Advising (A2.05e): Provide academic
counseling and faculty advising to students, including referral of
academic concerns as appropriate.
Remediation (A2.05f): Support the availability of
remedial instruction and participate in assigned student
remediation activities.
Curriculum (A2.05g): Participate in designing,
implementing, coordinating, and evaluating the curriculum.
Program Evaluation (A2.05h; C1.01): Participate
in program evaluation, self-assessment, and continuous improvement
activities.
Accreditation: Maintain familiarity with applicable
ARC-PA standards and participate in activities supporting ongoing
program compliance and accreditation.
Professional Development and Service: Engage in
scholarly and professional development activities and serve on
assigned program and University committees.
Position-Specific Responsibilities — Principal Faculty
Anatomy: Support the Director of Anatomy in the
planning, delivery, assessment, and continuous improvement of the
PA anatomy curriculum, including lecture and cadaver-based
laboratory instruction. Develop and deliver clinically integrated
instructional materials, laboratory activities, and student
assessments while assisting with course coordination and laboratory
preparation. Provide student academic support and help oversee
laboratory safety, professionalism, and compliance with applicable
OSHA requirements and institutional safety procedures.
Correlative Medicine: Coordinate the Correlative
Medicine course, including instruction, assessment, and course
evaluation.
Simulation: Lead assigned simulation activities under
the direction of the PA Program Simulation Coordinator, including
instruction, assessment, and coordination as needed.
Laboratory Instruction: Provide instruction and support
in History and Physical Examination and technical skills
laboratories.
Clinical Education: Support clinical-year activities
under the direction of the Clinical Director, including
orientation, callback days, student assessments, site visits,
preceptor orientation and development, and clinical curriculum
evaluation and improvement in collaboration with the clinical
education team.
Other Functions :
Conducts all work in a safe manner and ensures all work safety
practices are followed.
Performs similar or related work as required, directed, or as
the situation dictates.
Continues professional development and training; keeps current
with trends.
Assists other department staff as needed to promote a team
effort.
Knowledge, Ability, and Skill:
Demonstrated commitment to developing and fostering best
practices and policies to promote diversity, equity, and inclusion,
and build an environment in which all members of the University
community are treated with respect and dignity.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the
ability to interact professionally and effectively with students,
faculty, staff, and institutional and external stakeholders.
Strong organizational, time-management, and problem-solving
skills, including the ability to prioritize competing
responsibilities, adapt to changing needs, and meet
deadlines.
Ability to work independently, exercise sound professional
judgment, and demonstrate initiative and accountability.
Ability to collaborate effectively within the Physician
Assistant Institute and across the College of Health Sciences and
University.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and the ability to utilize
educational and administrative technology effectively.
Qualifications
Minimum Required Qualifications:
Education, Training, and Experience:
Master's degree required; doctoral degree preferred.
Minimum of two years of professional experience in clinical
practice, healthcare education, research, or a related field.
Academic preparation and professional experience appropriate to
assigned instructional and administrative responsibilities.
Three to five years of experience in PA education, higher
education, or academic administration preferred.
Special Requirements:
Physician assistant preferred; other appropriately qualified
healthcare professionals may be considered, consistent with program
staffing and accreditation requirements.
Must hold current, unrestricted professional licensure in
Connecticut or be eligible to obtain Connecticut licensure before
appointment, as applicable to the individual's professional
discipline.
Physician assistants serving in positions necessary to meet
ARC-PA PA principal faculty staffing requirements must maintain
current NCCPA certification or emeritus status.
Valid driver's license and access to an insured vehicle for
required program-related travel.
Full-Time Employee Benefits:

• Pet Insurance

• Employee & dependent life insurance

dependents
• PTO program

Job Description
Position Summaries:
Tenure-Track Assistant/ Associate Professor-MIP:
The Department of Microbiology, Immunology and Pathology at Colorado State University are pioneers in education, research, and clinical service programs that distinguishing our department as an international leader in human and animal health. MIP faculty collectively excel in basic and applied science and the integration of all related disciplines through programs in microbiology, immunology, pathology, infectious disease, cancer biology, prion biology, mycobacteria, vector-borne diseases, translational science, and diagnostic medicine. The impact of this expertise brings new knowledge to foundational science and clinical settings forging innovative discovery and patient care.
Tenure-Track Assistant/ Associate Professor-TMI/MIP:
The Translational Medicine Institute at Colorado State University is a multi-disciplinary research facility with a goal to improve the lives of humans and animals through biologic therapies created via the collaborative work of leading scientists and clinicians, to expedite the availability of these therapies, and to promote education related to these goals. Research within the Institute focuses on three major themes: Musculoskeletal Health and Repair, Infectious and Immune Disease, and Regenerative Medicine and Cellular Therapy. Under each theme are capabilities from our laboratories and research units. The Institute's success in improving the lives of patients who care for them is dependent on our principal investigators and faculty working in collaboration with these laboratories and units.
Overview:
Research: We seek research-intensive scientists who will establish vigorous, extramurally funded research programs whose expertise aligns and integrates with MIP's existing and emerging research strengths. Successful candidates will join a collaborative department with a strong record of scientific leadership, extensive shared infrastructure, and a deep commitment to training. We welcome applicants from any area of research that would complement and extend MIP's strengths.
We are particularly interested in candidates who use cutting-edge approaches that open new directions for the department and create bridges among its programs. These include, but are not limited to: New approach methodologies (NAMs), including organoids, organ-on-chip platforms, engineered tissues, and advanced in vitro and in silico systems; Data science and computational biology; Applied immunology; Biomarker discovery; and Molecular veterinary pathology. Candidates whose work connects to more than one of MIP's research communities, or whose research program can offer methodological expertise that colleagues across the department would draw on, will find an especially strong fit.
One of these positions is part of a cluster hire by the Translational Medicine Institute which spans multiple colleges including CVMBS. Applicants whose research interests align with the goal of this cluster hire (broad application areas of health and translational medicine) could be considered for this joint hiring opportunity.
Teaching: Teaching duties will be tailored to expertise and interests of the successful candidate, as well as the needs of the department (and TMI, in the case of the joint TMI-MIP hire). Teaching opportunities exist in the undergraduate, graduate, veterinary and human medical programs.
Service: Serve on departmental, college and university committees, particularly those related to research. Service to the broader national and international research community through participation in committee functions, editorial functions, symposia, grant review, and related activities.

jobs.title: Assistant Professors (Tenure-Track) in the Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering
jobs.description:
Assistant Professors (Tenure-Track) in the Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering at Louisiana State University
Louisiana State University (LSU) in Baton Rouge invites applications and nominations for twotenure-track faculty positions in the Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering (MIE) in the strategic research application areas of Advanced Construction (emphasis on Industrial Construction) and Manufacturing.
LSU is the Flagship University of the State of Louisiana with its main campus in the vibrant city of Baton Rouge, offering many cultural and recreational opportunities and high-quality housing.
MIE is the largest department in the College of Engineering in terms of on-campus programs with 33 faculty and instructors and 14 staff serving over 1500 undergraduate students and 130 graduate students on campus. Faculty research expenditures are over $9,5M over 120 active funded projects. The Department faculty provides leadership to several research centers & large federal grants, including (1) Future Use of Energy in Louisiana (FUEL) the NSF ENGINE, $160M, 10 yr award focusing on the Energy Transition; (2) The Louisiana Materials Design Alliance(LAMDA), a $20M, 5-yr cooperative agreement funded by the National Science Foundation (NSF) focusing on manufacturing process design for additive manufacturing (in metals, polymers and composites) using a model-make-measure paradigm enabled by machine-learning technologies and data science; (3) The NSF Industry/University Collaborative Research (I/UCRC) Center for Innovation in Structural Integrity Assurance (CISIA) with several industry members; (4) The LSU Institute for Energy Innovation, funded by Shell; (5) The P41 National Institutes of Health (NIH) Center for BioModular Multi-scale Systems for Precision Medicine as a partner to the University of Kansas, (6) The multi-institutional, multi-disciplinary NSF E-RISE RII: Use of a Louisiana Bio-Electric Fuel Incubator to Create Liquid Transportation Fuels from Agricultural Residues, (7) the NSF CREST Center for Next Generation Multifunctional Composites as a partner to Southern University, and (8) The National Center for Advanced Manufacturing (NCAM), a unique partnership between the State of Louisiana and NASA emphasizing large-scale manufacturing.
Associated research efforts leverage the Center for Computation and Technology (CCT) with formidable high-performance computing capability and relevant scientific research ecosystem, and the Center for Advanced Microstructures and Devices (CAMD), the only University-run synchrotron facility in the USA. An upcoming 150,000 sqft Construction and Advanced Manufacturing building reflects the investment of the College of Engineering and the University on the interdisciplinary application research areas targeted by this search. In addition, a new Robotics Engineering bachelor's degree will be introduced effective Fall 2027 in which MIE has a foundational role.
Appointments will be made at the Assistant Professor level, one in the mechanical engineeringprogram and one in the industrial engineering program, though applicants with exceptional qualifications may be considered at other ranks.
Research expectations include both the ability to successfully work independently and to pursue interdisciplinary collaborations; sustain an innovative, nationally recognized, and externally funded research and scholarly program; and growing relationships with industry.
Teaching expectations include a commitment to effective instruction and mentoring at the undergraduate and graduate levels, and supervision of student research.
Applicants with a bachelor's degree in mechanical, industrial, aerospace, nuclear engineering, or related discipline, will be considered for these positions. In addition, applicants should have aPh.D. in engineering or related scientific field (ABD candidates will be considered so long as degree requirements are met prior to the hire date), at least four years of experience, including graduate study, and excellent verbal and writing skills. Applicants with established research track records related to energy and/or defense applications will be prioritized.
We seek candidates who are prepared to apply advanced scientific skills, methods and technologies to the modeling, analysis, design, development, optimization, and improvement of complex engineered and socio-technical systems. Experience/Expertise is sought in any of the following subjects as related, or as applicable, to the targeted application research areas of Advanced Construction (emphasis on Industrial Construction) and Manufacturing:
• Development and Deployment of Robotic & Intelligent Systems: e.g. human-machine/robot-AIinteractive (smart collaborative) systems; coordinated autonomous multi-agent (e.g. multi-robot) systems; assistive, wearable, human performance augmenting systems; cyber-physical and networked robotics; robotics with integrated sensing and/or actuation with use-case customization.
• Advanced System Modeling Technologies and Methodologies: e.g. statistical simulation &inference, deterministic & stochastic optimization, robust optimization under uncertainty,resilience modeling, predictive & prescriptive analytics, data-driven decision-making.
• Digital Twins and Digital Construction: e.g. building information modeling (BIM), building assembly modeling (BAM), building operation optimization modeling (BOOM), virtual & augmented reality, reinforcement learning, operational behavior analysis, risk analysis.
• Cross-cutting experience straddling more than one of these subjects, and/or experience in applying modern approaches such as Artificial-Intelligence/Machine-Learning, Data Science(big data, analytics) and Cyber-Security to the targeted research application areas will be viewed very favorably.
An offer of employment is contingent on a satisfactory pre-employment background check.
The review of applications will begin on January 5, 2027 and will continue until the positions are filled. The expected start date for these positions is August 2027. Salary will be competitive based on qualifications. Campus interviews will be conducted in Baton Rouge, LA prior to an offer being extended.

The Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry at WKU invites applications for a full-time, nine-month, tenure-eligible appointment at the rank of Assistant Professor in any area of Analytical Chemistry, including Analytical Biochemistry, starting August 2027.
The Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry engages students at graduate (MS) and undergraduate levels, including the involvement of students from The Gatton Academy of Mathematics and Science, a nationally renowned residential high school. The University of Nebraska at Omaha ( UNO ) invites applications
and nominations for a tenured Associate Professor or Professor of
Early Childhood Inclusive Education who will also hold the
distinguished title of John T. Langan Chair of Early Childhood
Education in the College of Education Health and Human Sciences.

We seek an accomplished scholar, educator, and collaborative leader

The Langan Chair provides an exceptional opportunity for a scholar

preparation, and community engagement to improve opportunities and
outcomes for young children, particularly children with
disabilities and developmental differences and children and
families who have historically experienced barriers to
high-quality, inclusive early learning opportunities.
The Chair will be key UNO partner with the Buffett Early Childhood
Institute at the University of Nebraska, creating opportunities for
interdisciplinary and system-level collaboration in early childhood
research, practice, professional preparation, and community
engagement. The endowment establishing the Langan Chair
specifically provides for this affiliation and recognizes
excellence in teaching and research as central criteria for
appointment.
The University of Nebraska at Omaha is an Equal Opportunity
Employer, committed to preventing and eliminating discrimination
against employees and prospective employees based on race, color,

recruit, assess and select all candidates/employees using

treatment in our selection decisions and processes.

Varies

The successful candidate will be expected to maintain an active and
impactful program of research and scholarship in early childhood
inclusive education and related areas. The faculty member will
pursue external funding appropriate to their scholarly agenda;
disseminate research through high-quality peer-reviewed
publications and other influential scholarly and professional
outlets; and contribute to the national visibility and impact of
UNO’s work in early childhood education and inclusion.
The Langan Chair will also:
Lead the early childhood inclusive team with particular
attention to evidence-based approaches that support young children
with a range of abilities, developmental characteristics,
backgrounds, and learning needs.
Develop and sustain an innovative and nationally visible
program of research with potential to influence policy,
professional practice, educator preparation, and/or early childhood
systems.
Teach undergraduate and/or graduate courses in early childhood
inclusive education and related areas and contribute to the
preparation of highly qualified early childhood professionals.
Mentor undergraduate and graduate students and, where
appropriate, early-career faculty and emerging scholars.
Seek and secure external funding to advance research,
innovation, and collaborative initiatives.
Build interdisciplinary collaborations across UNO, Buffett
Early Childhood Institute and the University of Nebraska
system.
Establish and strengthen partnerships with early childhood
programs, schools, community organizations, families, state
agencies, and other partners to support inclusive opportunities for
young children.
Translate research into practice through partnerships with

communities.
Collaborate with the university, college, and units and NU

department, college, university, profession, and broader early

across the University of Nebraska. Of particular interest is a

early childhood education, but as a fundamental principle for
designing high-quality environments, professional preparation, and
systems in which all young children can participate, learn,
develop, and belong.
The successful candidate will have opportunities to build
collaborations spanning early childhood education, special
education, child development, family engagement, behavioral and
mental health, educational leadership, public policy, and related
disciplines. Through the Chair’s affiliation with the Buffett Early
Childhood Institute and engagement with community and state
partners, the faculty member will be positioned to connect rigorous
scholarship with meaningful improvements in practice and
systems.
