jobs.title: Tenure-Track Faculty Position in the Department of Information Systems
jobs.description:
The Department of Information Systems (IS) at UMBC invites applications for one tenure-track faculty position at the Assistant Professor level starting August 2027. We welcome applications from candidates engaged in high-quality research in Trustworthy AI, including but not limited to areas such as AI safety, robustness, security, and resilience; model governance, evaluation, verification, and uncertainty quantification; fairness, bias, and non-discrimination; and model transparency, auditability, and explainability. Applications from candidates whose research advances the trustworthiness of AI systems with interdisciplinary or real-world impact are particularly encouraged. Candidates' research interests should complement and extend our current strengths.
We are particularly interested in receiving applications from individuals who will contribute to UMBC’s mission and vision (https://umbc.edu/about/mission-and-vision) through their research, teaching, and service. Candidates must have earned a Ph.D. in a field related to the position no later than August 2027. More information about the research interests of our faculty can be found at https://informationsystems.umbc.edu/home/research.
The Department has 48 full-time faculty and over 2,000 students, including over 100 PhD students, making it the second-largest department at UMBC by both measures. The Department offers nine degree programs, including undergraduate degrees in Information Systems and Business Technology Administration. Graduate degree programs, MS and PhD, are offered in both Information Systems and Human-Centered Computing, including an innovative online MS program in IS. In addition, the Department houses the Master’s in Health Information Technology and the Master’s in Software Engineering, both as professional degree programs. Our faculty are actively engaged in collaborative interdisciplinary research within and across departments and institutions. Six of our current faculty have received NSF CAREER awards. IS faculty members lead six research centers: the Center for Real-time Distributed Sensing and Autonomy (CARDS), the Interactive Systems Research Center (ISRC), the NSF HDR Institute for Harnessing Data and Model Revolution in the Polar Regions (iHARP), the UMBC site of the Center for Accelerated Real Time Analytics (CARTA), the Center for Research in Use-Inspired Cyber-Physical Systems (CYPRESS), and the Center for Scalable Data and Computational Science (ScaleS). Further details can be found at https://informationsystems.umbc.edu/.
UMBC is an R1 public research university that is leading the world in inclusive excellence in research and teaching. UMBC is ranked #12 in 2024 among all U.S. universities in undergraduate teaching (US News). To continue to support this goal, the Center for the Advancement of Learning and Teaching (CALT) provides excellent support such as classroom observation, collection and analysis of student feedback, as well as regular workshops and pedagogical demonstrations. Our research is bold, cross-disciplinary, and leverages our location near government agencies, such as NIH, NASA, NSF, NIST, DOD, NIDILRR, NSA, DHS, DARPA, IARPA, ARL, ONR, and USGS.
UMBC’s strategic location in the Baltimore-Washington corridor puts us close to many high-tech companies and local area medical and nursing schools as well. The 2023 Chronicle of Higher Education also named UMBC as one of the great colleges to work for. The Department, College, and UMBC are deeply committed to the success of all of our faculty. We provide mentoring programs which offer regular and structured support for faculty to develop a thriving and successful research program, including launch committees for new faculty, and the Eminent Scholar mentoring program which helps faculty to build relationships with leaders in the field beyond UMBC. The campus is close to both energetic urban centers and family-friendly suburbs. Nearby cities such as Columbia and Ellicott City have been routinely ranked in the top 10 best places to live in the US by Money Magazine.
Candidates are expected to establish a collaborative, independent, externally funded, and nationally recognized research program in Trustworthy AI, and contribute to teaching a variety of graduate and undergraduate courses offered by the department. We expect candidates to be innovative in terms of pedagogical methods, course content, and curriculum development, and be committed to advising, mentoring, and supporting student success. All candidates are expected to demonstrate their commitment to UMBC’s mission and vision in all aspects of the position, including research, teaching, mentoring, service, and community engagement.
UMBC is a national model for inclusive excellence in STEM. Examples of these are our Meyerhoff Scholars Program (https://meyerhoff.umbc.edu/), the Center for Women in Technology (https://cwit.umbc.edu), PROMISE (https://gspd.umbc.edu/promise/), the Cyber Scholars Program (https://cybersecurity.umbc.edu/cyberscholars/), the CyberCorps: Scholarships for Service Program (https://cybersecurity.umbc.edu/scholarship-for-service-sfs/), and the McNair Scholars Program (https://mcnair.umbc.edu/). Inclusive excellence is a hallmark of UMBC and a foundational value of our community. UMBC is the nation’s #1 producer of Black undergraduates who go on to complete a Ph.D. in natural sciences or engineering and #1 for Black undergraduates who complete an M.D./Ph.D., based on NSF data.
The IS department is proud to support a diverse student and faculty body in terms of gender, race, and ethnicity. For example, our undergraduate student population is 32% female and 41% from underrepresented minority groups. The IS faculty has a culture of inclusive excellence, demonstrated both by academic research, such as community-engaged scholarship, research on improving accessibility of technology to individuals with disabilities, and by efforts to address diversity issues in STEM, such as the CWIT scholar program and a regional chapter of Women in Data Science and Machine Learning. Women faculty are leaders in the department and the college, directing centers and serving in leadership roles in the Dean’s office.
Applications for the position must be submitted as PDF files via Interfolio at https://apply.interfolio.com/195159. A complete submission will consist of:
1) Cover letter. Candidates need to address how their work (teaching, research, and service) aligns with UMBC's mission and vision.
2) CV
3) Statement of research interests (recommended length: two pages).
4) Statement of teaching philosophy (recommended length: one page).
5) Names and contact information of at least three references. Letters will be required later for short-listed candidates.
For inquiries, please email coeit-hiring@umbc.edu with Information Systems Trustworthy AI tenure-track 2027 hire in the subject line. Review of applications will begin in December 2026 and will continue until the position is filled.
Salary for this position is commensurate with experience, with a minimum of $120,000 and a maximum of $140,000. Other components of pay are offered when necessary to meet competitive conditions. The above salary range represents the University’s good faith and reasonable estimate of the range of possible compensation at the time of posting.
Nondiscrimination statement: UMBC does not make hiring decisions based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, or any other protected category under applicable federal law, state law, and the University’s nondiscrimination policy. We encourage applications from all candidates who meet the job qualifications and who will contribute to the University’s core value of inclusive excellence through their research, teaching, and service.

Le Moyne College, located in Syracuse, N.Y., is an independent college established by the Jesuits in 1946 to provide students with a values-based, comprehensive academic program designed to foster intellectual excellence and preparation for a life of leadership and service. Today, Le Moyne has evolved into a nationally acclaimed college of liberal arts and sciences that draws students from across the U.S. and abroad.

Le Moyne College is a diverse learning community that strives for academic excellence in the Catholic and Jesuit tradition through its comprehensive programs rooted in the liberal arts and sciences. Its emphasis is on education of the whole person and on the search for meaning and value as integral parts of the intellectual life. Le Moyne College seeks to prepare its members for leadership and service in their personal and professional lives to promote a more just society.
Le Moyne College aims to advance the values of diversity and inclusiveness at the college. To do this, Le Moyne seeks scholars and professionals who bring innovation, creativity, and impact to the campus, and who bring greater depth, breadth, and diversity to our campus community. Le Moyne College is an equal opportunity employer and encourages women, persons of color, and Jesuits to apply for employment.
Job Description
The M.S. program in Clinical Mental Health Counseling at Le Moyne College invites applications for a tenure-track position at the rank of Assistant Professor, to begin August 2027. We seek qualified candidates with a Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision who are dedicated to excellence in teaching with a commitment to a strong research agenda and service to the program, College, and profession. The typical teaching load is 21 credit hours over the year. This is a 12-month position. Teaching winter and summer courses may be required. Teaching responsibilities will include theoretical and clinical courses related to crisis, diagnosis, and supervision. Le Moyne College provides strong support for faculty research.

Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision by position start date.

About Le Moyne College
Located in Syracuse, N.Y., Le Moyne College is an independent college established by the Jesuits in 1946 to provide students with a values-based, comprehensive education designed to foster intellectual excellence and preparation for a life of leadership and service. Today, Le Moyne has evolved into a nationally acclaimed college of liberal arts and sciences that draws undergraduate and graduate students from across the U.S. and abroad.

Le Moyne College is a diverse learning community that strives for academic excellence in the Catholic and Jesuit tradition through its comprehensive programs rooted in the liberal arts and sciences. jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Mechanical Engineering Technology

jobs.title: Assistant Professor Tenure Track AY-Chemical and Biochemical Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Details
The Department of Chemical and Biochemical Engineering invites applications for a tenure-track position at the level of Assistant Professor. Applications from exceptional candidates at a higher rank will also be considered.
We seek outstanding candidates in the broad areas of pharmaceutical, biopharmaceutical, and advanced chemical processes and manufacturing, including experimental, computational, and data-driven approaches in these areas. Applications of particular interest include biomanufacturing; pharmaceutical process engineering, development, scale-up, and manufacturing; electrified and sustainable chemical processes; carbon circularity and industrial decarbonization; and waste upcycling and resource recovery. Computational and data-driven areas of interest include applied AI/ML and data science, self-driving laboratories and autonomous experimentation, digital twins, and advanced process monitoring, control, and optimization.
The successful candidate is expected to develop a strong, externally funded research program, contribute to existing and new teaching and training programs at the graduate and undergraduate levels in the field of Chemical and Biochemical Engineering, and provide service to the department, the school, and the university.
Applicants are expected to hold a doctoral degree in Chemical Engineering or a closely related discipline. The successful candidate will develop and sustain a research program leading to national and international recognition and demonstrate excellent communication, leadership, and collaboration in an interdisciplinary environment. Accomplishments appropriate to the candidate’s career stage will be considered.
About Rutgers Chemical and Biochemical Engineering
The Department of Chemical and Biochemical Engineering (CBE) includes 25 full-time faculty, more than 255 undergraduate students, and 110 graduate students. Located in central New Jersey, the department is situated in the heart of one of the nation’s leading pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and advanced manufacturing corridors, offering exceptional opportunities for research collaboration and engagement with industry. CBE faculty conduct interdisciplinary research in pharmaceutical engineering, biotechnology and biomanufacturing, energy and sustainability, materials, nanotechnology, and catalysis, as well as computational and data-driven approaches to chemical and biological systems. Faculty and students benefit from outstanding research facilities and collaborative opportunities through centers and institutes across Rutgers, including the Institute for Quantitative Biomedicine (IQB), Rutgers Climate & Energy Institute (RCEI), Center for Structured Organic Particulate Systems (C-SOPS), Catalyst Manufacturing Center, Rutgers Cancer Institute, RCSB Protein Data Bank, and New Jersey Advanced Manufacturing Institute. Rutgers Engineering faculty also have access to extensive high-performance computing resources for research and teaching. Learn more at cbe.rutgers.edu.
About Rutgers School of Engineering
Rutgers University–New Brunswick’s School of Engineering is home to educational opportunity and innovation, preparing a richly diverse body of nearly 6,000 undergraduate and graduate students to solve problems, make meaningful societal advances, lead through innovation, and excel in the global workplace. Ranked among the leading engineering programs in the nation, the school is centrally located in the Northeast Corridor amid a powerhouse of industrial, pharmaceutical, high-tech, transportation, and financial industries, providing professional and research opportunities. jobs.description:
Job Details
Purdue University Fort Wayne (PFW) School of Polytechnic invites applications for a nine­month tenure-track Assistant Professor of First-Year Engineering Technology position beginning August 2027.
A PhD in Engineering Technology or a related discipline is required.
Applicants should possess at least 3 years of relevant industrial experience or experience working with engineering technology student populations. Experience supporting student success, retention, transition, advising, or other first-year initiatives would be beneficial. The position involves regular communication and collaboration with students, faculty, and staff. Candidates should enjoy working closely with students, thrive in a small experiential classroom setting, and anticipate opportunities to collaborate with industry to strengthen the program.
Responsibilities include teaching and mentoring undergraduate students in the first year of Engineering Technology programs. The successful candidate will be expected to teach a variety of foundational courses that support student transition, engagement, and success in engineering technology disciplines, and potential courses matching the candidate’s expertise. Areas of instructional interest include, but are not limited to include freshman engineering technology, introductory engineering technology concepts, computer-aided design (CAD) for a broad range of majors, industrial practice, project-based learning, and related applied technical topics.

jobs.title: Associate/Full Professor of Atmospheric and Hydrologic Processes for Environmental Resilience
jobs.description:
Job Details
Associate/Full Professor of Atmospheric and Hydrologic Processes
for Environmental Resilience
Department: CAS Earth Sciences
Rank: Associate Professor
Annual Basis: 9 Month
Application Deadline
December 14, 2026; position open until filled
Required Application Materials
Complete applications include:
• A letter of interest that briefly expresses the candidate's
enthusiasm for the role and highlights their track record in
growing and strengthening community through collaborative efforts
and coalition-building.
• CV outlining work history and professional qualifications
relevant to this position.
• Statement of current and future research interests and
plans.
• Statement describing experience with inclusive teaching and
mentoring practices that promote students' success.
• Names and contact information for three professional
references.
Position Announcement
The Department of Earth Sciences at the University of Oregon
invites applications for an endowed Knight Chair in Atmospheric and
Hydrologic Processes for Environmental Resilience at the rank of
Associate or Full Professor. We seek an internationally recognized
scholar whose research advances fundamental understanding of
coupled atmospheric, hydrologic, and Earth-system processes and
applies that understanding to pressing environmental challenges.
The Knight Chair reflects the University of Oregon's commitment to
elevate and support scholarship that advances the public good. The
successful candidate will provide intellectual and collaborative
leadership in an area of substantial scientific and societal
importance, building a research program that advances fundamental
discovery while contributing to environmental resilience in Oregon,
the Pacific Northwest, and beyond.
We welcome candidates working broadly at the intersection of
atmospheric science, hydrology, climate science, and Earth-system
processes. Areas of research may include, but are not limited to,
atmospheric and land-surface interactions; extreme events, such as
atmospheric rivers, tropical storms, and marine heat waves; floods
and drought; wildfire, post-fire processes, and climate-fire
interactions; hydroclimate variability and change;
cryospheric-climate interactions; coastal processes; water
resources; cascading natural hazards; and interactions among
climate, hydrologic, ecological, and solid-Earth systems.
Climate-driven hazards, including intense storms, flooding,
wildfire, drought, coastal change, and landslides, are increasing
in consequence across the Pacific Northwest and globally, creating
an urgent need for predictive frameworks that connect atmospheric
dynamics with surface and subsurface hydrology and landscape
response.
We particularly encourage applicants who integrate innovative
approaches such as Earth-system and process-based modeling, data
science and machine learning, remote sensing, in situ observations
and sensor networks, field studies, or the synthesis of large
observational and computational datasets. The successful candidate
will have opportunities to connect these approaches to existing
University of Oregon expertise in hydrology, ocean and coastal
processes, cryospheric science, geomorphology, wildfire, landslides
and debris flows, earthquakes, volcanology, remote sensing, and
environmental data science. The department views the integration of
remote sensing, Earth-system models, machine learning, and field
observations as an important opportunity for understanding
interactions among climate, landscapes, hazards, and
communities.
The Knight Chair will be expected to maintain a vigorous,
externally funded research program; provide leadership in
interdisciplinary and multi-investigator research initiatives;
mentor graduate and undergraduate students; and teach courses at
the undergraduate and graduate levels. We seek a scholar who will
help shape new intellectual directions and partnerships across the
university and who values collaboration across disciplinary
boundaries.
A central goal of the position is to connect outstanding
fundamental scholarship with meaningful societal outcomes,
advancing knowledge in ways that benefit communities and contribute
to the public good. We therefore welcome candidates whose research
engages community organizations, agencies, Tribal Nations,
industry, policymakers, or other partners to improve understanding,
prediction, mitigation, adaptation, or resilience to environmental
change and natural hazards. The Knight Chair will have an
opportunity to build on the University of Oregon's substantial
expertise in hazards and environmental resilience while developing
new connections among atmospheric processes, water, landscapes,
infrastructure, and communities.
Department or Program Summary
The Department of Earth Sciences is an instructional and research
department within the University of Oregon's College of Arts and
Sciences, with internationally recognized programs spanning Earth,
environmental, and planetary sciences. Earth Sciences has a strong
record of externally supported research with more than $55 million
in external funding over the past decade and recent annual research
expenditures approaching $7 million. Research and graduate
education encompass geophysics and tectonics; volcanology,
petrology, and geochemistry; climate and cryospheric science;
oceanography; hydrology; geomorphology and surface processes;
paleontology and paleoecology; geobiology; and planetary
science.
The department has particular strengths in natural hazards and
environmental resilience through major collaborative programs and
centers focused on earthquake hazards, landslides and debris flows,
wildfire, volcanology, hydrology, ocean and coastal systems, and
land-surface processes. These strengths provide an exceptional
foundation for a senior scholar who can connect atmospheric and
hydrologic processes across Earth systems. Atmospheric and climate
processes currently represent a strategic opportunity for growth
and provide a critical link among many of these existing areas of
expertise.
Minimum Requirements
• Ph.D. in Earth Sciences or related field.
• Evidence of commitment to scholarly excellence, as seen in
peer-reviewed publications, grants, fellowships, and/or research
collaborations appropriate to their rank.
• A record of excellence in teaching, research/scholarship, and
service with credentials and accomplishments that meet the
standards for appointment as Associate Professor or Professor with
tenure
Preferred Qualifications
•Demonstrated intellectual and collaborative leadership in an area
of substantial scientific and societal importance.
• A record of leading successful interdisciplinary or
multi-investigator research efforts.
• Experience building research programs, shared resources, training
programs, institutes, centers, or other collaborative scientific
enterprises.
• A strong record of mentoring graduate students, postdoctoral
scholars, junior faculty, or other researchers.
• Evidence of effective and inclusive professional practices in
research, teaching, mentoring, leadership, and service
About the University
The University of Oregon is building a faculty committed to meeting
the needs of our changing student body and creating essential
knowledge for society. We encourage applications from individuals
who want to join an institution committed to addressing complex
problems at all scales, and critical thinking and
cross-disciplinary dialogue. We believe the way to create the
faculty we need is to develop the most inclusive applicant pool.
One of the goals of the University's strategic plan, titled Oregon
Rising, is to Create a Flourishing Community. As outlined in Oregon

every individual in our diverse community achieved through growth,
well-being, resilience, trust, belonging, robust connection, and
sense of purpose. A flourishing community is built on collective
experience and is made stronger by our shared commitment to one

All offers of employment are contingent upon successful

jobs.title: ME ASSISTANT PROFESSOR TENURE-TRACK FACULTY POSITION
jobs.description:
The Department of Mechanical Engineering (ME) at the University of Iowa (UI) invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Manufacturing and Artificial Intelligence (AI), starting in Fall 2027. We seek candidates with a strong background in manufacturing research. Research integrating AI with physical manufacturing processes and systems is of particular interest.
The successful candidate will advance manufacturing science and engineering through research grounded in physical experimentation and manufacturing process knowledge, with opportunities to integrate AI. We are interested in candidates who design and conduct experiments, develop or use manufacturing equipment and instrumentation, and validate research advances on physical manufacturing processes or systems. Candidates applying AI or machine learning should demonstrate a substantive connection to experimental manufacturing research. Candidates working across a broad range of manufacturing processes, materials, and applications are encouraged to apply.
Research areas of interest include, but are not limited to:
Advanced manufacturing processes and equipment. In-process sensing, monitoring, and process control to improve manufacturing quality, reliability, and productivity. Materials processing and experimental investigation of process–structure–property relationships. Physical robotic systems and manufacturing automation. Intelligent manufacturing and autonomous experimentation involving physical manufacturing processes and systems.
This position will strengthen manufacturing research and education in ME and connect manufacturing with complementary departmental strengths in design, thermal sciences, smart materials, robotics, and AI. ME is a vibrant, collegial, research-active department. The successful candidate will have opportunities to pursue interdisciplinary collaborations across the College of Engineering and the University of Iowa. Candidates with complementary research interests in interdisciplinary and emerging manufacturing applications are especially encouraged to apply.
Successful candidates should demonstrate potential for attracting external funding and establishing a nationally recognized research program in manufacturing. The successful candidate will develop a teaching portfolio in mechanical engineering courses, mentor undergraduate and graduate students, and contribute to departmental, university, and professional service.
ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT
The Department of Mechanical Engineering at the University of Iowa offers an engaging environment for education, research, and innovation. Our ABET-accredited undergraduate program provides a strong foundation in mechanical engineering, with four focus areas: Design, Energy and Environment, Manufacturing, and Robotics and Autonomous Systems. Through elective courses in these areas, students develop advanced knowledge aligned with their interests and career goals, preparing them for professional practice and graduate study. The department’s research spans robotics and autonomous systems, assistive technologies, smart multifunctional materials, multiscale computational science and engineering, artificial intelligence, advanced manufacturing, and marine science and ship hydrodynamics.
The College is committed to recruiting and retaining talented faculty and staff by providing competitive benefits, dual-career support, and resources that support building a successful career while enjoying a high quality of life in the Iowa City area. Through the University’s “Build a Career and Build a Life” resources, faculty and staff have access to programs and services that support personal well-being and work-life integration.
For best consideration, applications should be received by January 15, 2027. Review of applications will begin on January 19, 2027. Preliminary inquiries are encouraged and may be directed to Prof. Hongtao Ding at hongtao-ding@uiowa.edu.
Required Qualifications
A Ph.D. in mechanical engineering, industrial engineering, electrical engineering, manufacturing engineering, materials science and engineering, or a related discipline at the time of appointment. Evidence of success in securing, or strong competitiveness for securing, external research funding from federal agencies, industry partners, or other sponsors, and the ability to establish and sustain an independent research program that advances manufacturing science and engineering. Ability to teach and develop courses and mentor students in the Mechanical Engineering program.
Desired Qualifications
Commitment to teaching at every level of the mechanical engineering curriculum. Demonstrated potential for excellence in teaching and mentoring students. Ability to make significant teaching contributions in manufacturing. Experience advising student organizations, undergraduate researchers, competition teams, or design teams. Interest in curriculum development, educational innovation, assessment, engineering education scholarship, and/or engineering education research. Demonstrated ability to contribute to a welcoming and respectful learning environment.
The Application Package
To apply, visit https://jobs.uiowa.edu, select the faculty section, and search for requisition 76093. Submit the following materials:
Cover letter CV Research statement Teaching statement Names and contact information for three references.
Successful candidates will be required to self-disclose any misconduct history or pending research misconduct investigation including but not limited to sexual misconduct in prior employment and provide a related release and will be subject to a criminal background and credential check.
For H-1B petitions subject to the September 19, 2025, Presidential Proclamation, please note that the department will not cover the $100,000 payment associated with H-1B sponsorship, either at the time of hire or for international travel purposes. We encourage impacted individuals to explore alternative pathways for work authorization. Our team is available to help identify options that may be suitable for your situation.

jobs.institution: New York University, Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development
jobs.description:
Job Details
New York University’s Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in Counseling for Mental Health and Wellness to begin in September 2027. The appointed faculty member will be a member of the Department of Applied Psychology. The Master’s in Counseling for Mental Health and Wellness program trains future professional clinical counselors to understand people across the lifespan in cultural contexts, promotes equity and social justice in the work, and helps all people craft lives of wellness, health, and meaning. The applicant will also be associated with the Clinical/Counseling Psychology PhD program, which focuses on social justice-oriented education and training. We seek applicants who can bring clinical expertise to the MA program to train the next generation of mental health counselors, as well as complement the research scholarship of the current faculty in the PhD program. Applicants in the following areas of scholarship are encouraged to apply, though these are not exhaustive: neurodiversity across the lifespan; serious mental illness and alternatives to coercive care; trauma and resilience; structural violence/systemic oppression and mental health; culturally-adapted evidence-based practice; substance use/addictive behaviors; clinical health psych (e.g. sleep, chronic illness, etc); digital mental health/scalable interventions; and aging/geropsychology.
NYU Steinhardt is a uniquely interdisciplinary school, committed to a holistic understanding of people and human development across the lifespan. NYU Steinhardt has one-of-a-kind integration of education, communication, health, and the arts, with eleven departments, seventeen research centers and institutes, nearly 300 full-time faculty and close to six thousand students.
Responsibilities: The successful candidate will conduct an active program of research including publications and extramural funding; teach in the MA in Counseling for Mental Health and Wellness program; and advise and mentor across the undergraduate and graduate programs. The successful candidate will actively serve the program, Department, School, and University.
NYU's dynamic Global Network University includes NYU Abu Dhabi, NYU Shanghai, and international programs and academic centers around the world. NYU Steinhardt faculty may have the opportunity to engage in research and teaching at these global study and research sites.
Qualifications: Candidates should have a doctorate (e.g. PhD, PsyD, EdD) in clinical or counseling psychology or a closely related field and should be licensed (or license-eligible) as a psychologist. Preference will be given to applicants who have a strong research profile (including a history of securing extramural funding) and experience with clinical education with clinicians-in-training.
Application Instructions: Please submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae, research statement, teaching statement, and names and contact information of 3 references via the Interfolio system.
Review of applications begins immediately and continues until the search is complete.
Questions can be directed to Lisa Suzuki, PhD, Chair of the Search Committee, at las1@nyu.edu.
For more information on the MA in Counseling for Mental Health and Wellness, visit https://steinhardt.nyu.edu/programs/counseling-mental-health-and-wellness.
For more information on the Clinical/Counseling Psychology PhD program, visit https://steinhardt.nyu.edu/degree/phd-counseling-psychology.

Informatics – Associate Professor, Tenure Track
Location: Philadelphia, PA
Open Date: Nov 20, 2026

The Department of Biostatistics, Epidemiology and Informatics at
the Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania
seeks candidates for several Associate Professor positions in the
tenure track. Expertise is required in the specific area of
biomedical AI and informatics methods development and applications.
Relevant areas of particular interest include, but not limited to,
multimodal AI, agentic AI, and generative AI for biomedicine, as
well as clinical informatics, with applications to advancing
biomedical discovery and healthcare delivery. Candidates at this
level are expected to have an established research program and
successful track record of extramural funding. Applicants must have
a Ph.D. or equivalent degree.
Teaching responsibilities may include participation in biomedical
informatics and computational biology PhD and MS training programs,
as well as teaching informatics, data science and AI/ML courses in
biomedical graduate programs. Candidates are expected to have a
strong commitment to teaching and mentoring.
Research or scholarship responsibilities may include development of
innovative leading-edge AI and informatics methodology, with
secondary emphasis on collaborative research projects within the
Perelman School of Medicine and/or across Penn Schools. A
demonstrated track record as the principal investigator of
methodological research supported by extramural grant funding is
required. There is a rich mix of ongoing biomedical research
programs in the Perelman School of Medicine to provide motivation
and opportunities for the development of novel AI and informatics
methods on wide-ranging domains of biomedical, clinical, and
translational science.
The University of Pennsylvania is a vibrant team-science-oriented
environment with elite biomedical research collaborators. It is an
ideal environment for biomedical informatics collaboration and
application-driven methodological research. The primary faculty in
the Division of Informatics have strengths that span the
development, evaluation, and application of cutting-edge

biomedical sciences and healthcare. The Informatics Division is
part of a large department, with dozens of highly collaborative
faculty who specialize in biostatistics and epidemiology. The
successful candidate can also become a member of the Institute for

range of biomedical and clinical research applications.

family physicians in addressing the nation's maternal health
needs.

with the potential to become a national leader in primary

Position Description
Texas State
University seeks applications for open-rank professor
positions to conduct research on any aspect of aging and dementia
research. Texas State University is a leader in aging and dementia
with strengths in interdisciplinary social and behavioral dementia
research, translational and community-engaged research, caregiving,
ethics and autonomy in aging, environmental research and community
design, physical therapy and cognitive psychology.
Texas State is home to a robust community already working across
disciplines, the Alliance of Researchers in Aging (ARIA). ARIA
supports networking opportunities and interdisciplinary research in
aging, including research on cognition, cognitive decline and
dementia, mental health, care-giving, and physical, social and
spiritual well-being. Texas State also offers a Master of Science
degree in Dementia and Aging Studies with three tracks: 1) Dementia
and Long-Term Care, 2) Practitioner and 3) Researcher.
Texas State University receives a full share of the Texas
University Fund (TUF) and plans to invest funds in recruitment and
substantial start-up support for strategic hires with established
research programs and active external funding in historic and
emerging areas of research strength, including in aging and
dementia research. Texas State University hosted a town hall on
April 8 to discuss areas of impact for hiring in aging and dementia
research and to bring together the aging and dementia research
community.

teaching

Scope of Job:
We seek applicants who are dedicated to serving The
University of Texas Rio Grande Valley's student body as
Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor of Physics beginning in the
2027-2028 academic year. This is a joint appointment, with 80% of
the appointment in the Department of Physics and Astronomy and 20%
in the Department of Human Genetics. The successful candidate will
establish and sustain an independent, externally funded research
program in Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) Physics.
Responsibilities may include the conception, development,
validation, and application of novel MR methods; development of
specialized MRI approaches, hardware, or pulse sequences;
interpretation and dissemination of research findings; and
collaboration with faculty in Physics and Astronomy, Human
Genetics, and related disciplines. The successful candidate is
expected to lead an independent research program in MRI physics
centered on one or more coherent themes such as pulse-sequence
development and optimization, quantitative MRI, magnetic resonance
spectroscopy, rapid and accelerated imaging, MR fingerprinting,
diffusion encoding and biophysical modeling, susceptibility-based
methods, perfusion and vascular MRI, functional MRI physics,
artifact minimization, B0/B1 field characterization and correction,
MRI hardware and instrumentation, reproducibility, quality
assurance, or other MRI-related research topics of their interest.
The candidate will be able to leverage the Department of Human
Genetics' research-dedicated Siemens MAGNETOM Vida 3T system while
expanding its broader research potential beyond phenotyping and
genetics applications. The successful candidate will contribute to
collaborative research programs in Physics and Astronomy and Human
Genetics, including genetics phenotyping and MRI analysis, while
advancing MRI methods that benefit both departments. The faculty
member will teach courses consistent with departmental needs and
expertise; mentor undergraduate students, graduate students, and
postdoctoral scholars; contribute to curriculum and course
development; participate in departmental and university service;
and collaborate on interdisciplinary grant proposals and scholarly
publications. About UTRGV: UTRGV serves the Rio
Grande Valley and beyond via an innovative and unique multicultural
education dedicated to student access and success. By championing
leading research, healthcare, and application of university
discoveries, we support sustainable development, community
engagement, and well-being. The University of Texas Rio Grande
Valley (UTRGV) is committed to building and sustaining a highly
qualified and talented faculty to pursue excellence in everything
that we do, including teaching, research, and service. Drawing on
our unique identity as the leading Hispanic-Serving Institution in
a bilingual and bicultural environment, UTRGV will promote student
access and success by building from strength in education and
creating a vibrant campus experience. By 2027, we will accelerate
transformation in the Rio Grande Valley and beyond by driving
meaningful advancements in research and creative works, expanding
access to high-quality and affordable healthcare, and fostering
authentic community engagement and integration. UTRGV is a
distributed campus, one university spanning four counties and
multiple locations. Our purpose is to be a university for the
entire Rio Grande Valley and beyond. Over 91% of the students
enrolled at UTRGV identify as Hispanic, making UTRGV one of the top
3 universities with the highest percentage of Hispanic students.
For additional information, please visit UTRGV
website. Department of Physics and
Astronomy The Department of Physics and Astronomy at UTRGV
has tenure-track and tenured faculty members and several lecturers,
postdoctoral scholars, research and visiting faculty members
actively engaged in research in the areas of Applied Optics,
Biophysics, Computational Physics, Gravitational Wave Astronomy,
Nanotechnology, Optical Astronomy, Physics Education, Radio
Astronomy, Relativistic Astrophysics, and experimental Atomic,
Molecular, and Optical (AMO) Physics, including quantum optics,
single-photon optics, and quantum information science. Besides
excellence in research and teaching, the department places special
emphasis on early involvement of undergraduate and graduate
students in research. Integration of research and education at all
stages is one of the strengths of the department. The department
places emphasis on high-quality teaching and student mentoring. The
department has strong, well-funded research programs, and faculty
members have research collaborations with scientists across the
globe. Researchers in the Department of Physics and Astronomy
maintain state-of-the-art facilities, including a Pioneer-Two
electron beam lithography and scanning electron microscope,
electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy system, physical
property measurement system, cryogenic testing, RF measurement and
design facilities, laser and optics laboratories, and metal, ABS,
and resin 3D printers. Six state-of-the-art laboratories are funded
by the NSF, NASA, DoD, US Air Force, and NIH. The Department
currently has 26 tenured/tenure-track faculty members and 18
professional-track faculty, 29 graduate students, and 3
postdoctoral scholars. The department offers BS, MSIS, and PhD
degrees. Department of Human Genetics The
Department of Human Genetics has diverse research efforts in the
areas of diabetes, obesity, heart disease, ocular health,
psychiatric disease, osteoporosis, and infectious diseases of
border health relevance such as Chagas disease and tuberculosis. It
has state-of-the-art laboratories and genetic research
capabilities, including a 12,000-processor computer cluster
dedicated to genetic analysis, a biorepository containing tens of
thousands of samples collected in its numerous studies of complex
disease, and a colony of the unique animal model Monodelphis
domestica, and a state-of-the-art Magnetic Resonance Imaging 3T
system, fully dedicated to research. The Department of Human
Genetics focuses on the study of basic principles of genetics and
genomics as applied to human disease. Using both experimental
models and population-based approaches, it has ongoing programs of
research in experimental genomics, statistical and population-based
genetics, bioinformatics, imaging, and translational research. As a
comprehensive interdisciplinary unit housed within the UTRGV
College of Sciences, it has generated substantial extramural
funding for many years. The Department is home to a Ph.D. program
in Human Genetics, which recruits up to seven students per
year.
Minimum Qualifications:
PhD in Physics or closely related areas, with emphasis on magnetic
resonance imaging. Candidates must possess credentials appropriate
to teach assigned Physics courses in accordance with institutional
and SACSCOC faculty-qualification requirements.
Discipline Specific Required Qualifications:
Expertise in MRI physics.
Preferred Qualification:
Experience in MRI physics, sequence development, and image
reconstruction techniques.

Experience

jobs.title: Associate Professor and Program Director, Clinical Mental Health Counseling
jobs.description:
Job Details
Associate Professor and Program Director, Clinical Mental Health
Counseling
Florida Gulf Coast University
Job Summary
The School of Behavioral Health and Social Services within the
Marieb College of Health & Human Services at Florida Gulf Coast
University invites applications for a full-time, continuing
twelve-month Associate Professor and Program Director position in
the Clinical Mental Health Counseling (CMHC) Program beginning
August 2027.
The Program Director serves as the academic and administrative
leader of the CACREP-accredited Clinical Mental Health Counseling
Program and is responsible for program administration,
accreditation compliance, assessment, curriculum oversight, field
experience, faculty leadership, student success initiatives, and
continuous quality improvement. The successful candidate will
provide strategic leadership for the program while maintaining
excellence in teaching, scholarship, and service consistent with
expectations for the Associate Professor rank.
The Program Director works collaboratively with faculty, staff,
clinical partners, and university administrators to advance the
mission of the School, support student success, and prepare highly
qualified professional counselors to meet the behavioral health
needs of Southwest Florida and beyond. The position carries faculty
status at the Associate Professor rank with administrative
responsibilities associated with program leadership.
FGCU is building a culture of curiosity, commitment and
collaboration. We value employees who successfully work with others
and drive positive change through critical thinking and decisive
action. If you thrive in an environment of innovation,
accountability and mutual respect, you will find a good home
here.
Job Description
Typical duties include but are not limited to:
Program Leadership and Administration
Provide academic and administrative leadership for the Clinical
Mental Health Counseling Program.
Ensure compliance with CACREP standards and coordinate all
accreditation-related activities, including reporting, assessment,
self-studies, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Lead program planning, strategic initiatives, and long-range
program development.
Collaborate with the School Director on budgeting, enrollment
management, faculty workload, scheduling, staffing, and resource
allocation.
Coordinate student learning outcome assessment activities and
facilitate data-informed decision making.
Monitor student recruitment, retention, progression,
graduation, licensure outcomes, and program effectiveness.
Oversee admissions processes, student progression reviews,
graduation eligibility, and graduation certification
activities.
Prepare annual reports and maintain records required by the
University, College, School, and accrediting bodies.
Support faculty development, mentoring, and evaluation
processes.
Lead the recruitment, onboarding, mentoring, and support of
adjunct faculty.
Provide recommendations to the School Director regarding
faculty teaching assignments and instructional needs to support
student success and program effectiveness.
Facilitate program meetings and foster effective communication
among faculty, students, and stakeholders.
Address complex student concerns, complaints, appeals, and
collaborate with faculty to support student success.
Maintain partnerships with community agencies, clinical sites,
alumni, and professional organizations.
Work collaboratively with practicum and internship coordinators
to ensure high-quality clinical training experiences and compliance
with CACREP clinical training requirements.
Lead curriculum design, review, revision, and implementation to
ensure alignment with CACREP standards, professional counseling
competencies, regulatory requirements, and workforce needs.
Lead accreditation self-studies, annual reports, site visit
preparation, and continuous quality improvement activities.
Represent the program within the School, College, University,
and professional communities.
Teaching Responsibilities
Teach graduate counseling courses within the Clinical Mental
Health Counseling curriculum while providing leadership and
administrative oversight of the program. Faculty workload will
include reassigned time consistent with Program Director
responsibilities.
Develop and maintain high-quality instructional materials and
learning experiences aligned with CACREP standards and state
licensure requirements.
Provide mentoring and academic advising for graduate
students.
Participate in curriculum development and curricular
innovation.
Scholarship
Maintain an active scholarly agenda consistent with
expectations for appointment and promotion at the rank of Associate
Professor.
Disseminate scholarly work through peer-reviewed publications,
presentations, grant activity, and other professional
contributions.
Support student and faculty scholarship initiatives when
appropriate.
Contribute to the advancement of counseling knowledge and
practice.
Service
Participate actively in School, College, and University
governance.
Contribute leadership and expertise to professional counseling
organizations.
Engage in community partnerships and service activities that
advance the profession and support regional workforce needs.
Support initiatives that enhance student success, community
engagement, and academic excellence.
Other Duties
Adhere to University policies, procedures, and the Collective
Bargaining Agreement.
Perform other duties as assigned.
Additional Job Description
Required Qualifications:
Earned doctorate in Counselor Education and Supervision from a
CACREP-accredited program, or closely related field or qualified to
serve as core counselor education faculty under current CACREP
accreditation standards.
Experience and qualifications that commensurate with
appointment at the rank of Associate Professor.
Demonstrated record of scholarship consistent with expectations
for a tenured Associate Professor.
Experience with CACREP accreditation standards, assessment
processes, and program evaluation.
Demonstrated record of effective graduate teaching.
Experience in academic leadership, administration, or program
coordination within higher education.
Clinical experience relevant to Clinical Mental Health
Counseling.
Licensed or license-eligible mental health professional.
Preferred Qualifications:
Experience serving as Program Director, Department Chair,
Associate Chair, Graduate Coordinator, or similar academic
leadership role.
Experience leading CACREP accreditation self-studies, annual
reports, reaffirmation processes, or site visits.
Eligibility for licensure as a Licensed Mental Health Counselor
(LMHC) in Florida.
Experience supervising practicum and internship training.
Experience mentoring junior faculty.
Record of external funding, grant activity, or
community-engaged scholarship.
Experience developing partnerships with behavioral health
agencies and community organizations.
Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:
Knowledge of CACREP standards and counselor education best
practices.
Knowledge of counselor preparation, clinical supervision,
assessment, and accreditation processes.
Knowledge of major concepts, assumptions, debates, processes of
inquiry, and ways of knowing that are central to the
discipline(s).
Understanding how to use digital and interactive technologies
for efficiently and effectively achieving specific learning
goals.
Knowledge of critical thinking processes and understanding how
to help learners develop high level questioning skills.
Knowledge and skill in the use of inquiry-based instructional
models and strategies.
Ability to efficiently use computer applications and web-based
tools to complete work tasks
Ability to communicate clearly and effectively, both in writing
and verbally
Knowledge and ability to use technology in various teaching
modalities (e.g. Face-to-face, synchronous online or asynchronous
online).
Ability to collaborate with stakeholders both within and
outside the University in the development and delivery of
instruction, resulting in improved student learning.
Ability to contribute to our recruitment, retention, and
support students
Proven ability to think strategically and approach challenges
with creativity.
Demonstrated track record of reliability, meeting goals, and
holding oneself accountable.
Strong interpersonal skills and experience working effectively
across teams.
Institutional Values & Behavioral Expectations:
In this role, the successful candidate will be expected to:
Seek out new approaches to improve outcomes; remain open to
feedback and new ideas.
Lead with integrity; consistently produce high-quality work;
persevere to overcome obstacles to meet deadlines and achieve
deliverables.
Share information and insights thoughtfully; build partnerships
across departments; communicate respectfully; support colleagues to
achieve common goals.
Special Instructions to Applicants:
Appointment will be made on a 12-month multi-year appointment basis
with an anticipated start date of August 2027.
Because applications and materials are subject to public review and
retention under Florida's Public Records Law, please DO NOT send
examples of your project/ scholarship unless requested to do so.
Therefore, all submitted materials including articles, disks,
slides, books, etc., become the property of FGCU and CANNOT BE
RETURNED. As applicable, finalists will be notified of the need to
submit specific additional materials. Such materials will become
the property of FGCU. Under Florida's Public Records law,
applications will be available for public review upon
request.
Required Application Materials
Unofficial Transcripts
Statement of Teaching Philosophy
Curriculum Vitae
Cover Letter
Statement of Scholarship
Five (5) Professional References
Copy of counselor licensure
Review of applicant materials will begin immediately and
continue until the position is filled.
FGCU is a State University System of Florida member and an Equal
Opportunity and Equal Access employer. All qualified applicants
will receive consideration for employment without regard to race,
color, religion, sex, age, national origin, disability, or
protected veteran status.
To apply, please visit: https://jobs.fgcu.edu/jobs/associate-professor-and-program-director-clinical-mental-health-counseling-fort-myers-florida-united-states

CSUN's Commitment to You:
CSUN is committed to achieving excellence through teaching,
scholarship, learning and inclusion. Our values include a respect
for all people, building partnerships with the community and the
encouragement of innovation, experimentation, and creativity. CSUN
strives to cultivate a community in which a diverse population can

equity and inclusion in the pursuit of excellence for all members
of the university community.
As a Hispanic-serving Institution (HSI), inclusiveness and
diversity are integral to CSUN's commitment to excellence in
teaching, research, and engagement. As of Fall 2025, CSUN enrolls

Position:
The Department of Civil Engineering and Construction Management at
California State University, Northridge (CSUN) is seeking a
tenure-track faculty member in Construction Management at the rank

Ph.D. and B.S. in Construction Management, Construction

Evidence of effective engagement OR potential to engage with a

Experience using culturally responsive pedagogy that leads to

Experience creating a student-centered learning

Research/Lab experience that includes working with students

jobs.description:
Assistant, Associate, Full Professor (Tenured/Tenure-Track) in
Computer Science
College/School/Unit: College of Natural Sciences
Department: Department of Computer Science
Posted: Sep 22, 2026
Apply By: May 31, 2027
Description
The Department of Computer Science at The University of Texas at
Austin invites applications for tenure-track faculty positions. We
are accepting applications from outstanding candidates in all areas
of computer science.
In addition to all core areas within CS, we encourage candidates
with strong technical grounding in computer science whose work
creates opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration,
including potential partial or joint appointments in other
departments at The University of Texas at Austin. As part of UT
Austin's School of Computing, Computer Science has close ties with
the Department of Statistics and Data Sciences and the Department
of Information, creating additional opportunities for joint
appointments and cross-disciplinary research. We are also
particularly interested in candidates advancing AI for Science, as
well as those working specifically at the intersection of computer
science with neuroscience, biology, or medicine.
All interdisciplinary candidates are encouraged to send
applications to all relevant departments for better university-wide
coordination. Candidates working at the intersection of CS and
Neuroscience are particularly encouraged to send applications to
both departments to facilitate an explicit joint search. Candidates
may also apply to the Neuroscience position via Interfolio
(apply.interfolio.com/193043).
All positions are subject to the availability of funding.
The department is ranked among the top computer science departments
in the country. It has 64 tenured and tenure-track faculty members
across all areas of computer science. Beginning in Fall 2026,
Computer Science will be one of three founding academic units in UT
Austin's new School of Computing, alongside Statistics and Data
Science and Information. The new School is designed to strengthen
collaboration and create new opportunities for cross-departmental
research and education. Many faculty also participate in
interdisciplinary programs and centers across the University,
including Texas Robotics, the Machine Learning Laboratory, the
Institute on Foundations of Machine Learning (an NSF AI Institute),
Learning Directed Operating Systems (NSF Expeditions in Computing),
the Center for Generative AI, the Good Systems Grand Challenge on
Ethical AI, the Texas Advanced Computing Center (TACC), and the
Oden Institute for Computational Engineering and Science.
Austin, the capital of Texas, is a major technology hub, home to
significant operations from companies such as such as Amazon, AMD,
Apple, Applied Materials, AT&T, Dell, Google, IBM, Meta,
NVIDIA, Samsung, Silicon Labs, and Tesla. For more information
about the department, please visit https://cs.utexas.edu.
Qualifications
All tenure-track positions require a Ph.D. or equivalent degree in
computer science or a related area at the time of employment.
Successful candidates are expected to pursue an active research
program, to teach both graduate and undergraduate courses, and to
supervise graduate students in research.
Application Instructions
All faculty positions require a cover letter, current curriculum
vita, research statement, teaching statement and selected
publications. For all positions, applicants must provide the names
and contact information for at least three (3) references.
Confidential letters of recommendation will be requested directly
from the letter writers through Interfolio.
Review of applications will begin on December 1, 2026. Please apply
by then to ensure full consideration; however, the application
system may remain open after that time. Applications received after
the deadline are not guaranteed full consideration. Inquiries about
your application may be directed to faculty-search@cs.utexas.edu.
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
The University of Texas at Austin, as an equal
opportunity/affirmative action employer, complies with all
applicable federal and state laws regarding nondiscrimination and
affirmative action. The University is committed to a policy of
equal opportunity for all persons and does not discriminate on the
basis of race, color, national origin, age, marital status, sex,
sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, disability,
religion, or veteran status in employment, educational programs and
activities, and admissions.

jobs.title: Associate Vice President for Faculty Affairs
jobs.description:
Job Details
Associate Vice President for Faculty Affairs
CSUN's Commitment to You
CSUN is committed to achieving excellence through teaching,
scholarship, learning, and inclusion. Our values include a respect
for all people, building partnerships with the community, and
encouraging innovation, experimentation, and creativity. CSUN
strives to cultivate a community in which a diverse population can
learn and work in an atmosphere of civility and respect. CSUN
actively seeks candidates who make contributions to equity and
inclusion in the pursuit of excellence for all members of the
university community.
The University
One of the largest universities in the country, California State
University, Northridge (CSUN) is an urban, comprehensive university
that delivers award-winning undergraduate and graduate programs to
over 36,000 students annually and counts over 425,000 alumni who
fuel the region's economy. Since its founding in 1958, CSUN has
made a significant and long-term impact on California, generating
nearly $1.9 billion in economic impact and more than 12,000 jobs
each year. California State University, Northridge is a designated
Minority Serving and Hispanic Serving Institution (MSI/HSI) and a
California Black Serving Institution (BSI), nationally and
statewide recognized for advancing opportunity and promoting the
success of Hispanic, Black, African American, and other
historically underserved students. In 2025, Washington Monthly
named the university the No. 1 master's university in the nation
for contributions to the public good and ranked CSUN No. 2 Best
Bang for the Buck in the West and No. 3 Best Colleges for Your
Tuition and Tax Dollars. Also in 2025, the university earned a
4.5-star rating in Money's Best Colleges, ranked No. 3 for
diversity among public universities and No. 8 in the nation for
social mobility in The Wall Street Journal/College Pulse. In
addition, CSUN placed No. 9 on the California Mobility Index for
advancing economic and social mobility from the College Futures
Foundation.
About the Position of Associate Vice President for Faculty
Affairs
The Associate Vice President for Faculty Affairs (AVP FA) serves as
the University's academic personnel officer for faculty (Unit 3)
and academic student employees (Unit 11). Reporting to the Provost
and Vice President for Academic Affairs, the AVP FA provides
strategic leadership and administrative oversight for all faculty
lifecycle matters, including recruitment, appointment, evaluation,
retention, tenure, promotion, compensation, leaves, retirement, and
faculty professional success. The AVP FA ensures compliance with
collective bargaining agreements, CSU policies, and applicable
state and federal regulations while advancing equity, diversity,
inclusion, and belonging in all academic personnel processes.
As a member of the Academic Affairs leadership team, the AVP FA
advises the Provost, deans, and department chairs on complex
faculty personnel and labor relations matters. The AVP FA
interprets and implements collective bargaining agreements,
oversees grievance and disciplinary processes, conducts or
supervises investigations as appropriate, and represents the
University in labor management and arbitration proceedings. The
position works closely with Human Resources, Equity and Compliance,
and shared governance bodies to ensure fair, consistent, and
legally sound personnel practices. This role requires sound
judgment, collaborative leadership, and the ability to balance
institutional priorities with faculty interests in a dynamic higher
education environment.
As a leader, the AVP will have the opportunity to thrive in a
community in which our leaders share common traits as identified in
our Leadership Principles https://www.csun.edu/leadership-principles.
Qualifications
Required qualifications:
Earned doctorate or other terminal degree from an accredited
institution
Credentials and experience for appointment at the rank of
Professor
Demonstrated record of excellence in university teaching and
scholarly or creative achievement
Minimum of three (3) years of administrative experience as
department chair, director, associate dean, dean, or equivalent
leadership role
Demonstrated ability to interpret, apply, and communicate
complex policies and procedures
Demonstrated commitment to advancing equity, diversity,
inclusion, belonging, and accessibility in higher education
Demonstrated ability to handle sensitive and confidential
matters with sound judgment, integrity, and professionalism
Excellent written, oral, and interpersonal communication
skills, including collaborating with campus partners, building
trust, and facilitating shared governance
Preferred qualifications:
Demonstrated experience overseeing faculty personnel processes,
including recruitment, evaluation, retention, tenure, and
promotion
Demonstrated experience interpreting and implementing
collective bargaining agreements in a unionized higher education
environment
Demonstrated experience administering or advising on grievance,
disciplinary, or conflict resolution processes
Demonstrated experience collaborating with human resources,
equity/compliance offices, or legal counsel on personnel
matters
Demonstrated experience supporting equity-focused initiatives
in faculty hiring, evaluation, and retention
Demonstrated experience mentoring faculty and supporting
department chair leadership development
Demonstrated experience supervising professional staff and
managing administrative budgets while upholding staff welfare
through dignity- and respect-centered supervision
Demonstrated experience representing an institution in
systemwide committees or external relations
Demonstrated experience leading organizational change, process
improvement, or modernization of administrative systems
More information can be found in the institutional profile at
https://www.academicsearch.org/open-searches-
public/entry/25728/?search=25728
Pay, Benefits, & Work Schedule
Salary is commensurate with knowledge, skills, and experience. The
University offers excellent fringe benefits. The anticipated
HIRING RANGE: $190,000 to $210,000 per year, dependent upon
qualifications and experience.
Application Period
The position is open until filled but only applications received by
Monday, September 28, 2026, can be assured full
consideration. Review of applications will continue until position
is filled.
In order to be considered in the initial review, applications must
be submitted prior to the date listed above. Application
submissions received after the initial review date will be reviewed
at the discretion of the University.
Effective Date of Appointment: January 2, 2027
How to Apply
The university is being assisted by Academic Search. Applications
should consist of a substantive cover letter, a CV, and a list of
five professional references with full contact information. No
references will be contacted without the explicit permission of the
candidate. Applications can be confidentially submitted at:
CSUNAVPFA@academicsearch.org.
Nominations and expressions of interest can be directed to the
search team, electronically and confidentially, at: CSUNAVPFA@academicsearch.org.
Confidential discussions about this opportunity may be arranged by
contacting senior consultant Chris Butler at: Chris.Butler@academicsearch.org.
Background check
This position is a sensitive position as designated by the
CSU.
A background check (including a criminal records check) must be
completed satisfactorily. Failure to satisfactorily complete the
background check may affect the status of candidates who apply for
the position.
CANRA
The person holding this position will be considered a 'limited
reporter' under the California Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting
Act and is required to comply with the requirements set forth in
CSU Executive Order 1083 as a condition of employment.
Conflict of Interest
This position is a "designated position" in the California State
University's Conflict of Interest Code. The successful candidate
accepting this position is required to file Conflict of Interest
forms subject to the regulations of the Fair Political Practices
Commission.
Please note: California State University,
Northridge (CSUN) is not currently sponsoring staff or management
positions for H-1B employment visas. Applicants must be authorized

Equal Employment Opportunity
CSUN is an Equal Opportunity Employer and prohibits discrimination

Gender Identity (including Nonbinary or Transgender), Gender
Expression, Genetic Information, Marital Status, Medical Condition,
Nationality, Pregnancy or related conditions, Race or Ethnicity
(including color, caste, or ancestry), Religion or Religious Creed,
Sex (including Sex Stereotyping or Sex Characteristics), Sexual

jobs.title: Chair, Department of Agriculture
jobs.description:
Job Details
Fort Hays State University (FHSU) is seeking applicants for Chair of the Department of Agriculture. The position is a 12-month appointment. Depending on qualifications, applicants will be evaluated for tenure and the rank of Full Professor upon hire. The successful candidate must have a distinguished record of teaching, research, and service with an understanding and appreciation for on-campus and online delivery systems. The Chair will also have excellent communication and organizational skills, have demonstrated leadership abilities, and understand the needs of faculty, staff, and students. Future directions for the Department will include conservation and precision agriculture, renovation of the agriculture education program, and explorations of new undergraduate and graduate degree offerings and certifications.
Minimum Qualifications:
Earned doctorate in agriculture or closely-related field;
A recent record of the items listed below in keeping with appointment to Full Professor:
- Teaching excellence;
- Commitment to student success;
- Research accomplishments;
- Service to the discipline and community.
Preferred Qualifications:
Successful academic administrative experience including both fiscal and supervisory responsibilities, especially within the field of agriculture;
Demonstrated success with student recruitment and retention initiatives;
Experience with formalized assessment;
Record of external funding through grants and/or donor fundraising;
Demonstrated success with online education.
Responsibilities
The Chair of the Department of Agriculture reports to the Dean of the Werth College of Science, Technology, and Mathematics. The Chair, in consultation with the Dean, is responsible for the management, operation, and development of the department, including:
Provide strategic direction and vision for the department.
Oversee curriculum development, assessment, and continuous improvement considering holistic student success initiatives and program review.
Ensure programs meet regulatory requirements.
Support innovation in teaching, research, and service activities.
Foster interdisciplinary collaboration across departments and colleges.
Recruit, hire, onboard, mentor, and evaluate faculty members including merit reviews.
Manage promotion, tenure, and post-tenure review processes.
Coordinate faculty workloads and teaching assignments including course scheduling.
Encourage faculty scholarship, grant activity, and professional development.
Address personnel issues, conflicts, and performance concerns.
Monitor enrollment trends and student retention.
Address student concerns and academic issues.
Assist with student recruitment and outreach activities.
Manage the department budget and other financial resources;
Lead student recruiting and retention efforts for the department;
Teach 6 credit hours per semester and 3 credit hours during the summer.
Initiate and facilitate donor fundraising;
Ensure department initiatives align with University and Regents goals and plans;
Participate in college and university service activities;
Rank: Preferred: Professor; Will consider: Associate Professor
Benefits: To review our competitive benefit package, please visit FHSU Benefits.
Appointment Date: July 2027. This position is an on-campus position, not eligible for remote assignments.
Priority Deadline: Review of applicants will being on or after November 4, 2026 and continue until the position is filled.
Application Process: To apply for this position, please visit FHSU Careers. Only electronic applications submitted through the webpage will be accepted.
Required Application Documents
Candidates should submit a single PDF containing:
Cover letter addressing experience, qualifications, and how the applicant is suited to the position;
Current curriculum vitae;
The names and contact information of at least three professional references.
If you have questions regarding the position, please contact:
Dr. Mark Arant
mearant@fhsu.edu
About the Department:
The Department of Agriculture has eight full-time faculty positions serving approximately 400 undergraduate students pursuing Bachelor of Science degrees in Agriculture or Agricultural Business with the latter available online. The Agriculture major includes options in Agricultural Education, Agronomy, Animal Science, Agricultural Leadership, Agricultural Communications, Business Agronomy, and General Agriculture. A partnership with the FHSU Robbins College of Business and Entrepreneurship resulted in a new “4+1” MBA program with an agriculture emphasis that launched in 2022. Teaching and research are supported by a 3,400-acre University Farm, which reports to the Werth College Dean’s Office. See www.fhsu.edu/agriculture for additional information.
About the College:
The Werth College of Science, Technology, and Mathematics was formed in 2015 by bringing together the departments of Agriculture, Applied Technology, Biological Sciences, Chemistry, Computer Science, Geosciences, Mathematics, and Physics. The college employs approximately 70 full-time faculty, 1250 undergraduate majors, and 50+ graduate students. It also makes significant contributions to the university’s General Education program and to the Kansas Academy of Mathematics and Science, which is an early-college program for high-achieving high-school students. Undergraduate students participate in technical, classroom, field, and lab experiences that many schools would reserve for graduate students. Our academic programs are innovative and our facilities are outstanding. The Werth College of Science, Technology, and Mathematics teachers embrace a one-on-one teaching and mentoring philosophy and provide robust research opportunities for our students.
Community of Hays
FHSU is located in Hays, a vibrant college town of approximately 20,000, located halfway between Kansas City and Denver on Interstate 70. Hays is the regional center for education, health care, professional services, shopping, culture, and recreation for the western half of Kansas. The community boasts excellent recreational programs and facilities, including the comprehensive Center for Health Improvement, Hays Aquatic Park, Smoky Hill Country Club, Hays Municipal Golf Course, and extensive walking, running, and biking trails. Hays is within 45 minutes of two large lakes that offer great opportunities for boating, fishing, and camping. The Hays Municipal Airport provides connecting service to Denver with several flights daily. The Hays community is home to excellent Pre-K and K-12, public and private schools. With over 60 restaurants, major retail outlets, a low unemployment rate, and very short commute times, the city provides a safe, welcoming, low-cost, high-quality living environment for the residents who call "Hays, America" home.
Notice of Non-discrimination: FHSU is committed to providing equal opportunity and access to its educational programs, employment, services, and activities in compliance with federal and state nondiscrimination laws. FHSU prohibits discrimination, harassment, and retaliation on the basis of race, color, national origin, ethnicity, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, and gender identity and expression), age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law in its programs, activities, admissions, or employment.
Background Check: Final candidate will have consented to and successfully completed a criminal background check.
Notice to KPERS retirees applying for a position: Recent legislation changes working-after-retirement rules for both you and your employer if you go back to work for a KPERS employer. Please contact your KPERS representative or www.kpers.org for further information on how this might affect you.

The University of Texas at Austin is seeking well-qualified,

The University of Texas at Austin offers an exceptional environment

The University of Texas at Austin is located in the capitol of

innovative city. The city has been consistently rated a national
creative center that draws talented people from across the world to
its high quality of life, abundant resources, lively entertainment,
and active lifestyle. As an added benefit, the children of

Assistant Professor - Department of Management #27-04
